Shanghai Transportation
Shanghai, as the most modern international metropolis in China, has an all-round development of transportation system. No matter where you are now – overseas or in other parts of China – there are efficient and convenient transportation modes you can choose to reach Shanghai, and the diverse transportation options within the city also contribute to a worry-free Shanghai journey for you.
How to Get to Shanghai?
1. By Air – the Most Efficient Way to Arrive Shanghai from AfarSuppose your first destination in China is Shanghai, taking the plane is the most efficient way. Shanghai airports rank among the top three busiest airports in the world because of their wide coverage of airline service and dense air routes over the globe. At present, there are two airports in Shanghai – Pudong International Airport and Hongqiao International Airport, with the former being the major international aviation hub whose air routes are available in more than 130 cities overseas, and the latter mainly providing flight service in Chinese mainland mostly, as well as a few short-haul routes to Hong Kong, Macao, Taiwan, Japan, and South Korea.
By virtue of its extensive and convenient air service, Shanghai has constantly been the first stop when a large number of international tourists travel in China, as well as the transfer stop as many tourists travel to other Asian countries such as Japan and South Korea. Terminal of Shanghai Pudong International Airport  
2. By Bullet Train – More Efficient Option to Reach Shanghai within a Short-to-Medium Distance
Taking the bullet train can be a good choice if you depart from other Chinese cities to Shanghai, since 97% of Chinese cities have direct high-speed rail connections to Shanghai. In particular, if your departure location is not too far away from Shanghai, taking the high-speed train will be more cost-effective. For instance, it only takes 30 - 60 minutes to arrive Shanghai from its neighboring cities in the Yangtze River Delta including Suzhou, Hangzhou, Nanjing, etc. and 4 - 5 hours from central part of China like Beijing.
Nevertheless, the train journey from farther cities such as Xi'an and Chongqing to Shanghai takes a relatively longer time, approximately 6 hours. Therefore, if you have a tight schedule, you are more recommended to travel by air, which allows you to arrive in 2 - 2.5 hours.
Among all railway stations in the city, Shanghai Railway Station is the closest one to Shanghai downtown, followed by Shanghai South Railway Station and Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station. They all link with metro lines that can reach the Bund in 20 - 40 minutes. Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station Shanghai Bullet Trains 
 You may like:
West Railway Station 
East Railway Station 
3. By Cruise
Thanks to its advantageous location along the coast, Shanghai also has a well-developed maritime transportation system. The international cruise routes mainly include Japan, South Korea, and some Southeastern Asian countries such as Singapore and Malaysia and finally arrive at Shanghai Wusongkou International Cruise Terminal. Shanghai Cruise Shanghai Cruise on the Sea  
How to Get Around in Shanghai?
The transportation within Shanghai is efficient and travelers-friendly as well, with a diverse range of public transportation modes for you to pick. Subway, buses, and taxis all provide real-time service for you to visit various attractions and commercial districts; feature transportation like ferries, sightseeing buses, and the bund sightseeing tunnel are also available, not only facilitating your itinerary but also offering you unique experience to appreciate beautiful views of Shanghai.
1. By Metro
Taking the metro is preferred for traveling around Shanghai, especially during morning and evening peak hours on weekdays, which helps you in avoiding the traffic congestion on the roads. Besides, taking the subway is very economical, with a one-way fare ranging from CNY 3 to 26.
Currently, there are 20 metro lines in service in Shanghai. They not only connect the two airports and major railway stations, but also cover most attractions and commercial districts. For example, Shanghai Metro Line 1 links Hongqiao International Airport, Hongqiao Railway Station and the Bund; and Line 2 passes through Pudong International Airport, Shanghai Railway Station, Shanghai South Railway Station, People's Square, as well as Shanghai Tower, etc. Train Platform of Shanghai Metro Line 2 Inside Shanghai Metro Train 
  You may also want to know:
Shanghai Metro Maps
How to Take Shanghai Metro 
2. By Taxi Shanghai Taxi If you are burdened with luggage, then taking the taxi would be more comfortable, since taking the subway involves going back and forth between the station halls and the train platforms, as well as going through luggage security checks, which are inevitable. Moreover, traveling by taxi is one of the recommended modes during off-peak hours. Whether hailing a taxi by the roadside or ordering a taxi ride through the online platform, you can quickly board the vehicle and set off. Particularly if you want to visit some scenic spots in the suburbs of Shanghai, such as Zhujiajiao Water Town, whose entrance to the scenic area is about 15 minutes' walk from the nearest subway station, taking a taxi can send you directly to the destination.
The taxi fare in Shanghai is relatively reasonable. The cost for traveling between attractions within the city is approximately CNY 40 - 80 (USD 6 - 12), while the fare for going to the airport or more distant suburban attractions is about CNY 150 - 300 (USD 23 - 45). 
3. By BusThere are diverse buses in Shanghai, including City Bus, Sightseeing Bus, Tourist Bus, as well as Long-distance Bus.
City Bus: The city buses have extensive routes covering almost everywhere around Shanghai, serving as an alternative to the metro and perfectly making up for the inconvenience of some subway stations being a bit far from the entrance of certain tourist attractions. During off-peak hours, you may consider traveling by city bus, which helps you save money and also offer you convenience to admire the street views along the journey.
Sightseeing Bus: Shanghai boasts a lot of sightseeing buses, allowing you to visit the city’s landmark attractions in one go. What’s more, the buses are equipped with headphones that support multiple languages, making it easier for you to understand the history and fascinating stories behind different attractions. The most recommended sightseeing bus route is City Sightseeing Line 1, which connects the Bund, Lujiazui, Yu Garden, Nanjing Road, and People’s Square, among other core attractions. Shanghai Sightseeing Bus Shanghai Tourist Buses 
Tourist Bus: There are many tourist buses heading for scenic areas that are far away from the city center or located in some nearby cities. For instance, you can take the tourist bus from Shanghai South Railway Station directly to Shanghai Disneyland Park in 40 minutes at the cost of CNY 10, which is more time-saving and relaxing than taking the crowded metro. Besides, there are tourist buses from Shanghai Hongqiao Airport / Railway Station to Wuzhen Water Town operating four times each day, with the one-way ticket fare of CNY 55.
Long-distance Bus: If you are going to travel from Shanghai downtown to suburbs or its neighboring cities like Suzhou and Hangzhou, there are also long-distance buses for your consideration except for bullet trains.
4. By Ferry / Bund Sightseeing TunnelTaking ferry is the most cost-effective way to travel between the banks of the Huangpu River. For just CNY 2, you can get to the opposite bank in 10 minutes. As a bonus, you avoid the overcrowded entries / exits of the metro station, and gain an unforgettable experience to enjoy the fabulous river views. Additionally, if you want to visit Chongming Island, Changxing Island, or Hengsha Island near Shanghai downtown, you can also take the ferry.
The Bund Sightseeing Tunnel offers another way to travel between the two sides of the Huangpu River, providing a direct 3- to 5-minute passage to the opposite bank. As you go through the tunnel, you’ll experience fascinating visual and auditory effects that create a sensation of traveling through time and space. However, it’s somewhat more expensive, with a one-way fare of CNY 50.
5. By Shared BicycleWith pleasant weather, riding a bike to tour around Shanghai is really enjoyable, which helps you save energy and allows you to fully capture the multifarious scenery from place to place. The most recommended cycling route is the Greenway along the east bank of the Huangpu River, where you can take in the river views and landmarks of Shanghai such as the Bund Architectural Complex and the Oriental Pearl Tower. Shanghai Ferries Shanghai Shared Bicycles  
How to Pay for Public Transportation in Shanghai?
1. Using NFC PaymentIf your phone supports NFC payment, you can add your bank card such as UnionPay chip cards, Visa cards, Mastercards, American Express, and JCB contactless cards to the Wallet application such Apple Pay on your phone. Just make sure that there is sufficient balance in your card and that low-value password-free payment works, and then you can pay for metro ride by swiping NFC.
2. By CashCash is the most direct way to pay for public transportation in Shanghai. However, you are advised to prepare some change in advance since payment for the bus fee is usually in a self-help way, CNY 2 per trip. As for buying metro tickets, there are self-service ticket machines in the station halls that accept only banknotes of denominations of CNY 5, 10, and 20. You can also buy the metro ticket at the manual service counter, which is available in every metro station hall.
3. Using Shanghai Public Transportation Card Shanghai Metro Three-Day Pass You can use Shanghai Public Transportation Card in any transportation scenario, including taking the metro and bus, and even the ferry and Shanghai taxi. The card comes in two varieties, one is purple that can only be used in Shanghai, and the other is red that is valid nationwide. Both cost CNY 20 each, and can be purchased in most metro stations.
4. Using Metro Day PassOne-day Travel Pass and Three-day Travel Pass are two types of metro tickets mostly suitable for travelers. They can be purchased both at self-service ticket machines and the manual service counters in most subway stations.
The One-day Travel Pass costs CNY 18 and can be used unlimited times within 24 hours; the Three-day Travel Pass costs CNY 45 and can be used unlimited times within 72 hours. You may decide which ticket to buy based on your stay in Shanghai.
5. WeChat / Alipay QR Code ScanningIf you have a WeChat or Alipay account with proper payment functionality, you will find it much easier to use any mode of transportation. First, add the ride codes for Shanghai Metro and city buses on the WeChat Ride mini-program or in the Transport section of Alipay. Then, simply open the corresponding ride code before boarding to pay the fare. For taking taxis, you can choose to order one online in the travel service section of the ride application, or scan the driver’s QR code after arriving at your destination for payment. Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport
Airport Code: SHA 
 Location: Hongqiao International Airport, abbreviated as SHA airport, is located at No.2550, Hongqiao Road, Changning District;
about 13 kilometers (8 miles) from the downtown area and 60 kilometers (37 miles) from Pudong Airport.
 Two Terminals: T1 for domestic and international flights; T2 for domestic flights

1. Time for Taking Flights
Arrive at the airport 2-3.5 hours before flight departure
Closing Time for Check-in: Domestic Flight: 40 mins. before takeoff; International Flight: 45 mins. before takeoff
Closing Time for Boarding: Domestic & International Flight: 15 mins. before take-off
 Self-service Machines 
2. Arrival & Departure Procedures in T1 & T2 of Hongqiao Airport
International Arrival: Inspection & Quarantine – Immigration Inspection – Luggage Claim – Customs – Leave the Airport
Domestic Arrival: Luggage Claim – Leave the Airport
International Departure: Check-in – Inspection & Quarantine – Customs – Immigration – Security Check – Waiting & Boarding
Domestic Departure: Check-in – Security Check – Waiting & Boarding
3. Transfer in Hongqiao Airport
 Minimum Connection Time: D refers to Domestic; I refers to International
Transfer in the Same Terminal: D ⇒ D: 1 hour, D ⇔ I: 1.5 hours
Transfer from T2 to T1: D ⇒ D: 2.5 hours, D ⇔ I: 3 hours
Guide Map of Transfer Procedures of T2
4. Transfer between Hongqiao Airport & Pudong Airport
 Minimum Connection Time: Get on the shuttle bus/metro 3 hours ahead of time for domestic flights; 4 hours ahead for international flights
 Prior Transportation Choices: Suburban Railway Airport Link Line & Shuttle Bus Line 1 & Metro Line 2 
 See more: How to Get from Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station to Pudong Airport

From T1: Beyond walking distance; take metro line 10
From T2: Walk around 600 meters (656 yards), 10 min.

They are operated at four main railway stations: Shanghai Railway Station, South Railway Station, West Railway Station, and Hongqiao Railway Station.

How to Buy Shanghai Train Tickets
1. From TravelChinaGuide by clicking the arrival destinations in the table above or using the search box on this page top. This is the most convenient way. 
2. From any railway station in mainland China, including the four in Shanghai. Remember to bring your passport, as real-name ticket policy is strictly implemented.
3. From ticket offices scattering all over China, even in some suburban areas. 
4. From the 12306.cn. This is the official website of China Railway Corporation, but you need a Chinese phone number to log in.
Tip: It is better to book the tickets in advance, especially during the peak travel time, such as  National Day and Chinese New Year. Because there is a great possibility that they will be sold out in minutes once available. Location Map of Railway Stations in Shanghai Four main railway stations are avaiable in the city center:
Shanghai Railway Station
Located at 303 of Moling Road in Zhabei District, Shanghai Train Station is an integrated station which provides all kinds of scheduled trains to large numbers of cities inland, such as Beijing, Xian, Chengdu, Nanjing, Hangzhou, and Harbin.  It also serves the overnight sleeper trains to Beijing and overnight sleepers to Xian.  Video of Shanghai Railway Station  
South Railway StationIt is the southern gate of the city which is connecting with the Pearl River Delta and other areas in southern China. Trains from there mainly leave for Guiyang, Changsha, Shenzhen, Xiamen, Nanchang, and other cities. Additionally, there are many scheduled intercity trains running from this station to Jinshan District. Shanghai South Railway Station  
Hongqiao Railway Station
Hongqiao Railway Station is a large-scale, multi-functional, integrated rail hub with advanced facilities and the high level of modernization. It serves high speed trains plus connections to flights, subways, city buses, coaches and taxis. Currently, this station mainly serves bullet trains to Beijing, Hangzhou, Nanjing, Suzhou, Wuxi, Fuzhou, Wenzhou, Nanchang, Xiamen, Guangzhou, Hong Kong and many other cities over China. Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station  
West Railway StationAlthough the smallest one of the four stations, the West Station is a modern transportation hub serving for high speed trains, the city metro, and the city bus. It . High speed trains passing through the West Station including those to/from Nanjing, Suzhou, Changzhou, Danyang, Huishan, Hefei, and Wuxi. 
East Railway StationScheduled to be put into use in 2027, East Railway Station will be the second largest train station in Shanghai. It is located near Shanghai Pudong International Airport. After completion, trains to/from Suzhou, Hangzhou, Chongqing, Chengdu, Yangzhou, Nanjing and more places will be operated.

Shanghai City-Bus
 More than 10 Shanghai bus companies operate about 1,600 city bus lines in downtown and suburbs, offering convenient alternatives to metro. These lines can be identified either by numbers or Chinese characters representing the terminals. Shanghai bus stops of most downtown lines are announced by automatic reporter in Mandarin, Shanghai dialect and English, while a small part are announced in Mandarin and Shanghai dialect only.
Shanghai City Bus Routes
1. Regular Downtown Lines: 1 to 992, Daqiao Line 3 to 6, Tunnel Line 1, 2, 3, 6 & 8
2. District/Regional Lines & Suburban Lines: Starting with Pudong, Jiading, Baoshan, Qingpu, Minhang, Fengxian, Songjiang…
 City Bus Terminal Station 
3. Cross-district Lines: Starting with Huzhu Express, Shangzhu, Shangshi, Nanchuan, Xinjia, Songmei, Songxin, Shenchong, Lianzhu, Nanqing, Huqingying…
4. Night Lines: 301 to 345, Xumin Special Line, Tunnel Night Line 1
5. Downtown Shuttle Bus: 1001 to 1849 to solve the last-kilometer commute to/from metro station, and transfer between main roads and communities.
6. Rush-hour Lines: 04 -1090, Songjiang Line 29, Daqiao Line 1, Lingang No.2, Qinghua Special Line, Singjiang No.29
7. Sightseeing Bus: City Sightseeing Lines by Spring Tour, Shanghai Bus Tours, Shencheng Sightseeing Bus …
8. Shanghai airport to city bus: Pudong Airport Shuttle Bus, Hongqiao Airport Shuttle Bus
9. Other categories: Hongqiao Transport Hub Line 1 & 4 to 10, Ferry Lines, Customized Line, BRT Nantuan Line, BRT Fengpu Line
10. Intercity Lines: K319 & routes starting with Bahe, Huliu, Taijia, Jiashan, Kunshan, Pinghu, Yangshan and Qingshang.  
Shanghai Bus Schedule
 Most bus routes start running from 05:30 – 06:30 and stop service at 19:30 – 21:30.
 Rush-hour Lines operate from 06:00 – 08:00 to 16:30 – 18:30.
 Night Lines are in operation from 23:00 to 05:30 the next day. 
Shanghai Bus Fare & How to Pay
The city bus fare varies a little according to the vehicle types. Most routes including the downtown lines, suburban lines, night lines and rush-hour lines charge CNY2. The downtown shuttle buses only cost CNY1.
Passengers need to prepare some loose change to insert coins or banknotes into the coin box, or swipe the Shanghai Public Transportation Card to pay.
Most cross-district lines charge by distance and the ticket price is CNY1-12. Conductors sell tickets on these city buses on which passengers must pay in cash. Getting on the Bus Inside a city bus  
Shanghai Sightseeing Bus
Tourists can have a general look at Puxi, Pudong by the double-decked City Sightseeing Lines 1, 2, 3 & 5. They can hop on and hop off to visit attractions including Nanjing Road, the Bund, People's Square, Yu Garden, Xintiandi and Shanghai Museum. There are also three lines of Big Bus Tours connecting must-gos in Shanghai.
Shanghai Tourist Bus
Shanghai direct tourist buses set off at the airport and popular sites in the city center, taking tourists to Wuzhen, West Lake, Lion Grove Garden, Humble Administrator’s Garden ...

Trams in Shanghai
Songjiang Tram Lines:Line T1 connects Canghua Road and Xinqiao, while line T2 is a loop line running around Songjiang University Town. Songjiang Tram Line T3 to T6 is under construction. Shanghai will have more tram lines in Fengxian District and Pudong New Area in the future.

Shanghai Ferry
The Huangpu River running through Shanghai, divides the city into two parts - Pudong New District (east of the river) and Puxi Area (west of the river). The three islands of Chongming, Changxing, and Hengsha under the jurisdiction of Shanghai are separated from the main by the Yangtze River. As a result, ferries play a very important role in the city's transportation.  
Huangpu River Ferry 
As many bridges, tunnels, and subways are built, people have much more choices when traveling across the Huangpu River. However, ferryboats with 100-year's history are still popular choices for pedestrians and cyclists because of their convenience and low price. At present, there are in total 17 ferry lines serving nearly 40 ferry stations along both sides of the Huangpu River, providing links between Pudong and Puxi.
 Ticket Price:
Pedestrians: CNY2; free for children under 6 or 1.3 meters (4.3 feet)
Cyclists: CNY2.8
Motorcyclists: CNY4
 Notes: 
1. All the ferry stations offer self-service ticketing, and the ticket can be paid for by Alipay, WeChat Pay, Shanghai Public Transportation Card or cash. For cash users, it is advised to prepare loose change in advance.
2. Within the same day, pedestrians and cyclists with Shanghai Public Transportation Card will enjoy a discount of CNY 1 on the second journey.

  Shanghai Ferry Terminal Entering the Pier  
Island Ferry
Changxing and Hengsha Islands of Baoshan District as well as Chongming Island can easily be reached by ferryboats. In Baoshan District on the mainland of Shanghai city, there are four main ports handling ferryboats to the ports of the three islands - Hengsha Port, Majiagang Port of Changxing, and three ports of Chongming, namely, Nanmen, Baozhen, and Xinhe. Detailed information on these ports is provided as follows:

Shanghai Sightseeing Ferry Huangpu River Ferry Among the 17 normal lines above, three lines are economic choices for sightseeing: Nanlu Line, Dongfu Line and Dongjin Line. Nanlu Line, also called Setting Sun Line by the citizens, offers the most amazing view and is more recommended. 
Besides, the sightseeing ferryboats of Shanghai provide you with a chance to experience the exciting Huangpu River cruise. The sightseeing ferries sail from Shiliupu Pier, Oriental Ferry Terminal and East Jinling Rd. Ferry Terminal, passing by the prosperous Lujiazui Financial District, Jinmao Tower, Shanghai World Financial Center, Yangpu Bridge, Garden Bridge, and the iconic architecture near the Bund. The ticket price is CNY120 – 130. It is recommended to take the night lines to enjoy the prosperity of the international metropolis.

Pudong New Area, Shanghai
Pudong New Area Facts
Chinese Name: 浦东新区 (pǔ dōng xīn qū)
Population: 5,501,000
Area: 1,210 square kilometers (467.2 square miles)
Location: in the east of Shanghai City, east China
Area Code: 021
Zip Code: 200120
GDP (2018): CNY 1,046 billion (USD 158.1 billion)
First Free Trade Pilot Zone in China
Pudong New Area is a municipal district of Shanghai City. Fengxian District and Minhang District are on its north. Xuhui District, Huangpu District, Hongkou District, Yangpu District and Baoshan District are to its west across the Huangpu River. Chongming District is on its north. Pudong New Area Shanghai is the first free trade pilot zone in China. It is rich in tourism attractions including Chuansha Ancient Town, Shanghai Wild Animal Park and the Oriental Pearl Radio & TV Tower.
Best Places to Visit & Top Things to Do in Pudong New AreaYou may need 1-2 days for Pudong New Area travel in modern skyscrapers, Chuansha Ancient Town, Shanghai Wild Animal Park, Shanghai Science Center and other tourism attractions.
Visit Modern Skyscrapers
 Skyscrapers in Pudong 
 Shanghai Tower
As the highest skyscraper in Shanghai, it is 632 meters (2,073 feet) high with 119 floors. Travelers can overlook the whole city on the 118th floor and enjoy the light show on holidays.
 Shanghai World Financial Center
Located in Lujiazui, it is 492 meters (1,614 feet) high with 101 floors above ground. Travelers can go sightseeing on 94th – 100th floor. And the high-speed elevator is with a maximum speed of 8 meters per second which only takes 66 seconds to the 95th floor.
 Oriental Pearl Tower
It is one of the iconic cultural landscapes in Shanghai. Travelers can have a full view of the city on the sightseeing floor, have delicious dishes in the revolving restaurant and experience the unique Shanghai culture in the exhibition hall.
 Jin Mao Tower
With 420.5 meters (1,780 feet) high, there are 88 floors of the main building and the sightseeing hall is on the top. The outer wall is made up of large glasses which reflect in different shades and colors.
Shanghai Wild Animal ParkIt is the first national grade wild zoo in China. Travelers can see more than 200 kinds of rare wild animals from home and abroad such as pandas, monkeys, zebras, and white rhinoceros. You should pay attention to that spring from March to May and autumn from September to November are the best time to visit safari park.
Chuansha Ancient TownChuansga is the hometown of Shanghai Opera, a gathering place for opera fans. With more than 500-year-history, Chuansha Ancient Town still remains an ancient wall from the Ming Dynasty (1368 – 1644). There is a great combination of western and Chinese elements, such as the Catholic Church which will leave you a deep impression.
Others: Long Museum
Best Time to Visit Pudong New AreaThe best time to visit Pudong New Area is from March to May and from September to November with a temperature of 15-21℃ (59-69.8℉). It is located in the coastal area where the East Asian monsoon prevails, and the climate in Pudong New Area Shanghai belongs to the subtropical monsoon climate. With distinct four seasons, there are abundant rainfalls, sufficient sunshine and suitable temperature. The annual average temperature is 16℃ (61℉). You should pay attention to that from April to September is the rainy season.
During March and May, the peach blossoms will be in full bloom, it is the best time to admire the beauty of flowers.
Pudong Weather Forecast
-
TransportationShanghai Pudong International Airport is located in Pudong New Area, about 40 km (24.9 mi) and Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport is about 30 km (18.6 mi) from the center area of Pudong New Area. Travelers can choose to take a flight to these two airports first and then take Metro Line 2 to Pudong New Area. Shanghai Railway Station and Shanghai South Railway Station are very close to Pudong New Area, travelers can take Metro Line 1 and transfer Line 2 after getting off the train.
Within the city area, Metro Line 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 16 are available. The taxi charges CNY 14 for the first 3 km, CNY 2.4/km for no more than 10 km, and CNY 3.6/km for subsequent distance. It may cost CNY 140-150 from Shanghai Pudong International Airport and CNY 60-70 from Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport to Pudong New Area.
 See more: Shanghai Metro, Shanghai Taxi
Pudong Food to TryThere are many delicious local foods in Pudong New Area including Sanlin Benggua, Gaoqiao Waffle, Pan-Fried Chicken Bun, and White Rabbit Sugar.
 Sanlin Benggua
This kind of melon is in an oblong shape with a weight of 1-1.5 kg. The melon rind is very thin and crispy. It is famous for its sweet taste.
 Gaoqiao Waffle
It is famous for its well-bedded pastries which are as thin as paper. It is shaped like a moon cake with a fragrant flavor, thin skin, various stuffing, crispy and soft taste.
 Pan-Fried Chicken Bun
With yellow sesame seeds and chopped green onion in the upper part, it tastes soft and palatable. And the lower part is crispier with heavy stuffing and juicy chicken.

Huangpu District, Shanghai
Huangpu District Facts
Chinese Name: 黄浦区 (huáng pǔ qū)
Population: 852,476
Area: 20.5 square kilometers (7.92 square miles)
Location: in the center of Shanghai, east China
Area Code: 021
Zip Code: 200001
GDP (2018): CNY2,270.31 billion (USD 343.10 billion)
Traditional City Center
Huangpu District, subordinate to Shanghai, is located in the southwest end of the confluence of Huangpu River and Suzhou River. It is close to Hongkou District and Yangpu District on the north, Luwan District on the south, Jing’an District on the west, and Pudong New Area on the east. It is one of the most prosperous and central areas of Shanghai where visitors can appreciate the wonderful cityscape. In addition, there are many Shanghai landmarks, old buildings and streets such as the Bund, Shanghai People's Square, Nanjing Road, Yu Garden and Shanghai Museum. It is better to spend 2-3 days to have an enjoyable Huangpu District travel.
Best Places to Visit & Top Things to Do in Huangpu District
 The Bund
Near to Huangpu River, the Bund is one of the must-see scenic spots in Huangpu District Shanghai with 33 buildings in different styles. Numerous skyscrapers that stand on the opposite side of the Huangpu River can be seen in the Bund, such as the Oriental Pearl Tower, Jin Mao Tower and  World Financial Center. At night, visitors can take a Huangpu River cruise at the Bund to enjoy the stunning night scenery.
 Nanjing Road
Nanjing Road is one of the ten famous pedestrian streets in China and the earliest commercial street established after the opening of Shanghai port. It is a shopping paradise as a lot of department stores gather here with a complete range of goods. Creative city sculptures are everywhere, and there are plenty of chairs in the middle of the street for visitors to relax. It's a good experience to ride a scaled-down version of the old tram which was the main transportation method in Shanghai before.
 Yu Garden
Built in the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644), Yu Garden is known as one of the five classical gardens in Shanghai with the exquisite pavilions, halls, rockeries, ponds and cloisters. The highlights of Yu Garden include the Great Rockery, Cuixiu Hall, Sansui Hall, Wanhua Chamber and Exquisite Jade Rock. On the outside of Yu Garden is Yuyuan Bazaar where visitors can buy souvenirs and taste delicious foods.
 Shanghai Museum
Shanghai Museum is a large museum of ancient Chinese art, with 12 special exhibition rooms and over 120,000 fine collections. The museum gathers historical relics of different dynasties, especially bronzes, chinaware, calligraphy and paintings. In addition, special exhibitions are often held in the museum, displaying various Chinese and foreign cultural relics, art works, calligraphy and paintings.
Best Time to Visit Huangpu District
The best time to visit Huangpu District Shanghai is March to May and October to November when the climate is relatively pleasant with the average temperature of 15℃ (59℉). Huangpu District China has four distinctive seasons. From July to August are the hottest months of the year and the highest temperature is 37℃ (97℉). December to February is the coldest period of the year with a temperature of 7℃ (45℉). The rainy season in Shanghai starts in the middle of June every year and lasts for a month. It is not a good time to have a Shanghai travel. 
Huangpu Weather Forecast
-
Transportation
Visitors can fly to Shanghai Pudong International Airport and then take Metro Line 2 to Huangpu District Shanghai or to Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport and then take Metro Line 10 to there. It is easy to reach there by bullet trains as the Shanghai Railway Station provides all kinds of scheduled trains.
Metro, buses and taxis are the main transportation means in Huangpu District Shanghai. The Shanghai Maglev Train also serves the public and visitors can reach the Shanghai Pudong International Airport in 40 minutes. Metro Line 1, 2, 4, 8, 9, 10 and 13 are available there. Visitors can take Metro Line 10 and 2 to get to the Bund and Nanjing Road. It is also recommended to take the Shanghai Sightseeing Bus for a one-day or two-day city tour. The starting price and charging standard of Shanghai taxi are different between day and night.
 See more: Shanghai Metro
Best Huangpu Food to Try
The best Huangpu District Shanghai foods to try are Steamed Buns, Pan Fried Pork Bun, Sweet Soup Balls, Ribs Rice Cakes and Shanghai Cuisine. And visitors can taste many local dishes or snacks in Yunnan South Road.
Shanghai Cuisine: It is characterized by using much oil and soy sauce to make moderate, original and mellow flavors. The popular dishes include Yan Du Xian Soup, Stewed Pork with Brown Sauce, Fried Prawns and Eight-treasure Delicious Duck.

Jing’an District, Shanghai
Jing’an District Facts
Chinese Name: 静安区 (jìng ān qū)
Population: 246,788
Area: 37 square kilometers (14 square miles)
Location: in the center of Shanghai, east China
Area Code: 021
Zip Code: 200040
GDP (2018): CNY184.7 billion (USD 27.9 billion)
One of the Core Urban Areas
Jing’an District is located in the center of Shanghai, adjacent to Huangpu District and Hongkou District on the east, Changning District and Putuo District on the west and Xuhui District on the south. "Jing’an" is named after the Jing’an Temple, a must-see scenic spot in Shanghai. It is an important window for Shanghai's foreign exchanges and rewarded the best leisure tourism destination by China National Tourism in 2018.
Best Places to Visit & Top Things to Do in Jing’an District
 Jing’an Temple
Jing’an Temple is a famous ancient temple in Shanghai. At present, the main buildings of the temple include the Shanmen (gate to the temple), Tianwang Hall, Daxiong Hall and Sansheng Hall. The silver Buddha enshrined in the Mahavira hall weighs as heavy as 15 tons. From a distance, the whole temple has a golden roof, particularly conspicuous. Jing’an Temple attracts many people to worship or visit. What’s more, the stunning and beautiful night view of the temple cannot be missed.
 Shanghai Natural History Museum
The Shanghai Natural History Museum displays tens of thousands of specimens. It has 5 floors and 10 permanent exhibitions, which are divided into three themes: natural evolution, life world and human civilization. What is most interesting is the skeleton of the 26-meter (85-feet) long Mamenchisaurus Sinocanadorum, the largest dinosaur in Asia with the longest neck in the world. The Exploration Center is children's favorite where they can experience the sense of achievement of digging fossils by themselves (Need an appointment in advance).
 Moller Villa
Moller Villa was a private garden villa owned by Moller, a wealthy Jewish businessman, and has transformed into Hengshan Moller Villa Hotel since 2005. The main building is a three-story house in Norwegian style. The interior decoration is very exquisite as beautiful and delicate patterns are carved everywhere. You can take photos in the hotel for free, or enjoy afternoon tea in the garden.
 Wujiang Road
With convenient transportation, Wujiang Road is a wonderful place for shopping, sightseeing and tasting delicious food. All kinds of special dishes and local snacks can be found there, among which the Xiaoyang Pan-Fried Bun Stuffed with Pork and Nanxiang Steamed Buns are the most famous.
 See more: 6 Best Food Streets in Shanghai 
Others: Jing’an Villa, Shanghai Exhibition Center
Best Time to Visit Jing’an DistrictThe best time to visit Jing’an District Shanghai is from September to November when the weather is clear and pleasing with the average temperatures of 21℃ (70℉). With dense buildings and a lack of green space, the city-centered Jing’an District is easy to form a heat island effect. So Jing’an District Shanghai has more hot days in summer from June to August and the average temperature is 28℃ (82℉). The winter time of Jing’an District, December to February, is about 7 ℃ (45℉). The rainy season in Shanghai starts in the middle of June every year and lasts for a month. It is not a good time to have a travel to Jing’an District during that time.
Jing’an Weather Forecast
- 
TransportationIt takes about 80 minutes from Shanghai Pudong International Airport by Metro Line 2 to Jing’an District Shanghai. Or visitors can take a flight to Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport and take Metro Line 2 to Jing’an District. Taking a bullet train is also available and visitors are able to reach Jing’an District Shanghai from Shanghai Railway Station in 35 minutes by Bus 927.
Metro Line 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8 and 13 are serving in Jing’an District Shanghai. Visitors can take Metro Line 2 and 7 to Jing’an Temple and Metro Line 1, 2, 12 and 13 to Shanghai Natural History Museum. The starting price and charging standard of Shanghai taxis are different between day and night. It charges CNY 170-180 to Pudong Airport, CNY 50-60 to Hongqiao Airport and and CNY 20-30 to Shanghai Railway Station. 
 See more: Shanghai Metro, Shanghai Taxi
Best Jing’an Food to TryThe best Jing’an District food to try are Wonton, Spring Rolls, Glutinous Rice Balls and Tonkotsu Ramen.

Shanghai Weather
Located in subtropical monsoon climate zone, Shanghai is relatively humid, and has four distinct seasons: pleasant and warm spring from March to May, stuffy and humid summer lasting long from June to September, comfortable and cool autumn from October to November, and overcast and a bit cold winter from December to February.  Shanghai Night View  
Temperature
There are big temperature differences between seasons: the temperature can reach above 35°C (95°F) in summer, drops to around 0°C (32°F) in winter, and stays around 10-25°C (50-77°F) in spring and autumn. Therefore, it is necessary to further check the detailed temperature situation of your planned travel dates. 
High/Low Temperatures of Shanghai
The Hottest Months of Shanghai
The hottest months of Shanghai are July and August with the daily high temperature generally above 30°C (86°F) and around 35°C (95°F), and the apparent temperature on some days is high at a level that may make you feel uncomfortable. Specifically, there are usually around 10 days when the high temperature is no less than 35°C (95°F) per month. It is not surprising at all if the daily maximum temperature exceeds 40°C (104°F) or above during this period. For example, in July and August 2024, Shanghai experienced three days when the daily high reached 40°C (104°F). 
The Coldest Month of Shanghai
The coldest month is January, but it is not severely cold here, when the daily high can reach 10 - 15°C (50-59°F) and the daily low is around 0 - 5°C (32-41°F). Even on the coldest day in this period, the temperature usually stays from -5°C (23°F) to 0°C (32°F). In some years, Shanghai may not see temperature below 0°C (23°F) at all.
Precipitation
The city receives high precipitation of around 1,200 mm annually, and it mainly concentrates in: (1) the plum rainy season from mid-June to early July, when Shanghai sees consistent rain, high humidity, and relatively short sunshine hours; and (2) the typhoon season from late July to September, when strong wind and heavy rain may hit Shanghai. The monthly average rainfall during these months ranges from 135 mm to 159 mm, and the number of rainy days per month exceeds 10. In the rainiest month of Shanghai, June, the rainy days are about 15. In other words, visiting Shanghai from June to September, there is a quite high possibility of being caught by rain.
Average Precipitation of Shanghai
Does it Snow in Shanghai?
In Shanghai, the probability of snow is low. The annual average snowy days are only about 1 to 5, concentrated from late December to the next February, with some years experiencing no snow at all. On these possible snowy days, light snow and sleet are more common. Besides, it’s hard for you to see snow cover in Shanghai due to the not low enough temperature.
Humidity
The air is relatively wet in Shanghai nearly all year round. On average, the humidity is no less than 70% every month. During the quite rainy period from June to September, the average humidity is around 75%. Such humidity levels produce some effect on apparent temperature: in summer, it makes you feel hotter and more stifling; in winter, it makes you feel clammy.
Humidity of Shanghai
Best Time to Visit Shanghai
Springtime, from March to May, and autumn, from October to November, are regarded as the best times to pay a visit to Shanghai. Traveling to Shanghai during these two periods, you will feel neither cold nor hot. Besides, you seldom encounter quite rainy weather in these months. As for the scenery, with colorful flowers or autumn leaves, it will not let you down.
If possible, when planning a Shanghai trip in 2026, avoid July to August with large travel crowds, scorching hot weather, and frequent summer showers.

Shanghai Climate - Seasons & Travel Recommendations
Spring: March - May
Weather: Spring in Shanghai is from March to May. This is one of the best seasons of the year for traveling. The temperature is at a comfortable level. Light rain happens, however, does not disturb your trip much. Spring flowers in bloom make the city lively and attractive.
Clothes: Most of the time, short-sleeved or long-sleeved shirts plus thin jackets and jeans are suitable outfits. However, in early March, relatively thick coats is necessary.
Travel Recommendations: With cozy temperature and mostly sunny climate of Shanghai, spring is a perfect time to both admire the cultural attractions like The Bund & Huangpu River and Jade Buddha Temple and explore the natural beauty like in Zhujiajiao Water Town. Pay attention to the occasional large temperature difference between day and night.
 See also: 15 Most Beautiful Places in Shanghai in Spring Lush Yu Garden in Spring 
Summer: June - September
Weather: Summer here is long from June to September. With high temperature and a lot of rainfall that accounts for over 50% of the city's annual total, Shanghai at this time can be uncomfortably hot and humid, especially in July and August, when the temperature reaches 35°C (95°F) or above quite often. 
Clothes: Wear clothes like breathable and lightweight tank tops, T-shirts, skirts, and shorts to keep cool in summer with high temperature and humidity. Besides, an umbrella is a must in rainy summer. Hot Summer with Intense Sunshine 
Travel Recommendations: Considering the heat, you are recommended to visit outdoor attractions in the early morning, late afternoon, and at night, the relatively cooler periods. As for the hottest period from about 12:00 to 14:00, you’d better visit indoor attractions like Shanghai Museum or just stay at hotels or restaurants to rest. 
 See also: 12 Popular Shanghai Activities to Survive Summer
Autumn: October - November
Weather: The short autumn comes in October and November. In this season, the weather turns cool and pleasant. The flood season has ended, and you will not experience much rain. In conclusion, the temperate weather makes this season a good travel time. 
Clothes: Long-sleeved shirts plus thin jackets are appropriate. Bringing a thicker coat when visiting Shanghai in late November is a clever decision. People Playing Taichi in Cool Autumn 
Travel Recommendations: With such wonderful weather conditions, you can enjoy a city tour comfortably, like taking a Huangpu River cruise to see western buildings of the Bund and modern skyscrapers in Lujiazui, visiting the busy Nanjing Road, and admiring the Yu Garden. If you travel to Shanghai in late autumn, you can see it decorated by the golden autumn leaves. 
 See also: Where to Go in Shanghai in Autumn - 11 Best Destinations
Winter: December - February
Weather: The city's temperature in winter is not as low as in northern China like Beijing, and the worst of the cold usually lasts for just a few days in late January, the only period when the daily low may drop below 0°C (32°F). However, humid cold wind may blow sometimes, making the apparent temperature much lower. Winter is the period with the lowest rainfall all year round, when Shanghai only sees a little rain or snow. A Bit Cold but Sunny Winter 
Clothes: Sweaters, thick pants, and thick overcoats like woolen coat are necessary. In the coldest January, down coats are more suitable. 
Travel Recommendations: The weather will not be very cold, and besides unmissable activities like viewing the classic Yu Garden under bright sunshine and modern Bund and Nanjing Road, you are also advised to visit Disney Winter Magic Cavalcade in Shanghai Disney Resort, and feel the festival atmosphere of the Chinese New Year.

Best Time to Visit Shanghai
Best Months to Visit Shanghai: March-May; October-NovemberMarch to May and October to November are the best times to visit Shanghai, since they boast cozy and favorable weather, vibrant and colorful scenery, and not very crowded attractions overall. View of the Bund  
March to MayShanghai gets rid of the damp and chilly winter and ushers in spring during this time. Temperatures rise to around 10-25°C (50-75°F), making for a warm and comfortable climate. You can enjoy outdoor sightseeing without bundling up in heavy layers or worrying about intense heat. Moreover, rain won’t pose much of a threat to your trip, as this season typically features light showers and enjoys plenty of sunshine. Furthermore, the city transforms into a veritable world of flowers, with cherry blossoms, tulips, magnolias, rapeseed flowers, and many other blooms filling the streets. 
During these months, as long as you avoid the Qingming Holiday in early April and May Day holiday in early May, you can experience Shanghai at its most romantic with a relatively quiet atmosphere. Zhujiajiao Water Town in Spring  
October to NovemberAt this time of year, Shanghai has completely shed the stifling heat of summer, with temperatures hovering between 15 and 22 degrees Celsius (59-72 degrees Fahrenheit) - an extremely comfortable range. Besides, both the rainy season and typhoon season have ended, and this period has minimal rainfall, dry air, and excellent visibility, making it ideal for all kinds of outdoor activities. Moreover, Shanghai offers a unique natural spectacle during this season: autumn foliage. With these golden leaves, attractions like the Yu Garden and Zhujiajiao Water Town become even more appealing.
Apart from the National Day holiday in early October, visitor numbers in Shanghai remain not very high during the rest of this period. Yu Garden in Early October  
Best Months to Enjoy a Quiet and Cheap Trip: December-February, Except the New Year and Chinese New Year Period 
These three winter months mark the slack tourism season of Shanghai. The biggest advantage of the off-season is, of course, that it offers a quieter and more relaxed experience thanks to fewer tourists. Specifically, visiting either the Bund or the Yu Garden during this time, you can enjoy your trip at a leisurely pace and don’t need to make any effort to dodge crowds while taking photos. Additionally, if you choose to visit Shanghai during these months, your overall travel costs will be significantly lower: hotel rates will be discounted, airfares will be cheaper, and attractions like the Yu Garden will offer off-season pricing.
The New Year period in late December, as well as the Chinese New Year Festival period in January or February, are not part of the off-season; on the contrary, these times are very crowded. If you are looking for a quiet trip, be sure to avoid these two periods. 
Note: This period is considered the slack season because the weather in Shanghai is quite cold. Therefore, be sure to pack plenty of warm clothing for your trip and do not stay outdoors too late in chilly evenings. Quiet Disneyland Park in Winter Yuyuan Bazaar with Fewer Tourists  
Not-Recommended Months to Visit Shanghai: Mid-June to Mid-September
First, this is the hot summer, with high temperature above 30°C (86°F) nearly every day, and usually around 35°C (95°F). Combined with high humidity, the weather feels uncomfortably hot. It’s no exaggeration to say that within half an hour of staying outside, you will feel sticky all over.
Second, Shanghai experiences frequent rain during this period. Mid-June through early July marks the city’s plum rainy season, when persistent drizzles and sudden downpours fall from time to time. Your itinerary will be significantly disturbed: outdoor sightseeing will be inconvenient, visibility will be low and the sky will almost always be overcast, and some shows and parades at Disneyland Park may be canceled. From late July to mid-September, Shanghai is likely to be affected by typhoons, which force you to stay indoors.
Furthermore, it’s important to note that Shanghai is packed with tourists in July and August, as this period coincides with China’s summer vacation. Inevitably, travel expenses will also be significantly higher than usual. Crowded Nanjing Road Even in Morning  
OK Months to Visit Shanghai: Early June & Late September
Though early June also belongs to summer, the climate of Shanghai is not very hot. Besides, the city has not entered the rainy season yet. In late September, the weather gradually cools down, and the typhoon season ends. So, these two periods both feature not bad weather conditions. 
The Most Crowded Periods You Should AvoidThe busiest travel periods you are highly recommended to avoid are the three long holidays - the Chinese New Year holiday in January or February, the May Day holiday from May 1 to 5, and the Chinese National Day holiday from October 1 to 7. How crowded will Shanghai be at these times? At popular attractions like the Bund, Nanjing Road, and the Yu Garden, you’ll practically be pushed along by the crowd; meanwhile, you’ll have to wait in line for two to three hours for the most popular items at Disneyland Park. In addition, hotel rates typically rise to two or three times their usual price.
New Year’s Day, Qingming Festival in early April, Dragon Boat Festival around mid-June, and Mid-Autumn Day in mid to late September are also full of visitors, though not as many as the above three holidays.

Shanghai Weather in January
 Shanghai is a bit cold in January, especially when the sun is absent. Besides, light rain falls sometimes, leading to colder climate. The not very friendly temperature makes January a low tourist season, so visitors can enjoy quieter attractions and more reasonable prices than usual, especially in mid-January.  Beautiful Night View of the Bund  
Cold Overall and ChangeableShanghai’s winter weather hits hardest in January. To be specific, Shanghai weather in January delivers a cold feeling, especially during the nighttime: the daily high temperature mainly ranges from 5 to 13 degrees Celsius (41-55 degrees Fahrenheit), while the daily low fluctuates between 0 and 7°C (32-45°F) most of the time. Besides, the high humidity and occasional chilly winds actually make one feel much colder than the digits indicate.
You should also know that this is not the whole story: there are also some extreme cold or warm situations that may occur this month. Occasionally, the city may encounter a sudden temperature drop, when the daily high and low are only 0°C (32°F) and -5°C (23°F), respectively, and you will feel quite cold. At the same time, cozy and warm days with the daily high and low of around 20°C (68°F) and 10°C (50°F) also exist. So, you are recommended to always keep a close eye on the weather forecast during your trip and bring clothes of various thicknesses. Cold Shanghai in January  
Low Precipitation, but High HumidityDue to the overall not low enough temperature, Shanghai rarely snows, but it rains. Shanghai receives about 11 rainy days on average in January, delivering only 43 mm of precipitation, one of the lowest levels throughout the year. The rain is usually small and doesn’t produce much inconvenience on your trip. Generally speaking, sunny and cloudy moments dominate this month.
The average humidity of Shanghai in January is high at around 72%. As mentioned earlier, this will lead to lower apparent temperature and make you feel damp and chilly.
Daylight Hours & Sunshine HoursWith late sunrise and early sunset, January only has about 10-10.5 hours of daylight. Therefore, you are advised to start the day early and arrange some nighttime tours to get a richer and more colorful trip.
Sunshine hours are about 4 per day on average, not long at all. Besides, sunlight is soft and UV rays can be ignored this month. You are recommended to take full use of these hours, when the climate tends to be warmer and attractions look more stunning, to visit outdoor spots.

Low Temperature: 1°C / 34°F
Humidity: 72%
Rainfall: 43 mm

Average AQI:62
Is January a Good Time to Visit Shanghai?
January is an OK month to visit Shanghai. 
First, though it is the month with the lowest temperature in Shanghai, you generally won’t feel unbearably cold. And, the climate of Shanghai at this time is relatively sunny.
Second, most of the time in January is the low season with far fewer visitors and quieter attractions, and hotel rates become considerably more affordable. Though you need to know that early month and late month are two exceptional periods with a significant influx of tourists: from January 1 to 3, the New Year holiday arrives, and by the month’s end, students gradually begin to enjoy their winter holiday. Quiet Yu Garden in January 
Third, in addition to visiting those always worth-visiting and beautiful attractions like the Bund and Jing’an Temple, Shanghai in January provides you with some unique and wonderful experiences:
Highlights of Shanghai in January 
1. Feeling the Atmosphere of the Chinese New Year
The Chinese New Year usually falls in January or February, and as early as January, many spots in Shanghai wear festival decorations. For instance, you can admire:
(1) Yu Garden Lantern Shows
In Yuyuan Bazaar, just outside the Yu Garden, the stunning Yu Garden Lantern Festival is held every year to celebrate the Chinese New Year. Various colorful and delicate lanterns in shapes of Chinese zodiac animals, flowers, etc., and illuminated Spring Festival couplets can be seen, showing a vibrant festival atmosphere. Yuyuan Bazaar with Lanterns 
(2) Festival Decorations and Shows in Zhujiajia Water Town and Panlong Tiandi
As the New Year approaches, Zhujiajiao Water Town is adorned with red lanterns everywhere, creating a unique and lively scene. Panlong Tiandi features an array of stunning lanterns of various shapes. Moreover, at both places, you will have the chance to witness festival performances like lion dances.
2. Admiring Special Natural Views in Winter
Beyond the festival decorations and activities mentioned above, this month’s natural scenery also holds a unique charm. 
(1) Limited-Time Flower Sea at North Bund
The Bund is definitely on your travel list. Visiting this spot in January, you will get a delightful surprise: at North Bund, tens of thousands of violets bloom in the chilly wind, weaving a dazzling sea of rose red, pale purple, and white flowers.
(2) Colorful Scene in Yu Garden
Though not as lush as summer, the Yu Garden in January remains full of life. First, evergreen trees within the grounds provide a backdrop of deep green. Second, some trees still bear yellow autumn leaves. Particularly noteworthy is that this month marks the peak blooming season for wintersweets, meaning that you can spot golden blossoms adorning the classical gardens. Wintersweets in the Yu Garden 
(3) Majestic Winter Sycamore Trees
Want to experience Shanghai’s winter atmosphere? You are recommended to take a stroll to admire the sycamore trees. In January, their leaves have all fallen, leaving only bare branches that evoke a crisp and quiet ambiance. Wuyi Road and Fuxing Middle Road are all good places to go.
What to Wear in Shanghai in January 2027?
Clothes: For the tops, you are recommended to wear a thick shirt plus a thin sweater, a hoodie, or a wool sweater as the inner layer. Then, wear a thin down coat or wool coat as the outer layer to keep warm. For the bottoms, fleece-lined jeans or sweatpants are both OK. If you are sensitive to coldness, consider packing long johns.
Shoes: Thick but comfortable casual shoes or boots are recommended to bring.
Others: Beautiful but warm hats and scarves are better to be brought to protect yourself from the occasional cold winds. Prepare an umbrella with you in case the occasional rain wets your clothes and makes you feel colder.
Tips for Visiting Shanghai in January1. Early reservations for hotels and attraction tickets are needed, especially if your travel dates are during early and late January, to guarantee a smooth trip. 
2. Wear thick and warm enough clothes for a night tour, especially when cruising on the Huangpu River.
3. Want to see more lovely wintersweets? Zhenru Park won’t disappoint you - it boasts over 60 varieties and more than 1,000 wintersweets blooming since mid-January.

Shanghai Weather in February
 Shanghai suffers from damp and relatively cold air in February. Rainy days account for more than 10 days on average, but the good news is that there are rarely heavy or long-term rains. As long as you can endure a little low temperature, you can have a relatively good tour in February, when Shanghai is surrounded by decorations for the Chinese New Year and flowers like plum blossoms.
TemperatureAs a winter month in Shanghai, February features relatively cold weather. On most days, the daytime has a temperature range of 6-15 degrees Celsius (43-59 degrees Fahrenheit), and the nighttime experiences a colder climate with the temperature of 0-10°C (32-50°F).  Cold February 
The temperature in February is somewhat unstable. The first half of the month may have very cold days, though in rare instances, with daily highs dipping below 5°C (41°F) and lows potentially falling below 0°C (32°F). Conversely, the latter half of the month occasionally sees quite warm days with daily highs exceeding 20°C (68°F).
All in all, you are recommended to pay attention to the weather forecast and bring enough clothes to deal with the temperature fluctuations.
Apparent Temperature May Be Lower.Sometimes, the apparent temperature is much lower than the weather forecast tells. On the one hand, the humidity is relatively high and averages at around 71%. As a result, the air feels uncomfortably clammy and colder. On the other hand, winds sweep Shanghai occasionally in February, which tend to be stronger in riverside areas like the Bund, making the apparent temperature 3-5°C (5-9°F) lower.
PrecipitationThere are about 12 rainy days on average in Shanghai in February. However, you should not be discouraged by this number. Actually, the monthly precipitation averages only 60 mm, and the rain is usually light or lasts for a short period, meaning that it won’t influence your trip a lot. Sleet may fall this month, but only with a small chance. 
Days with or after precipitation are usually colder, so wear more if you go out for a visit on those days. Colder Rainy Days of Shanghai in February  
Daylight Hours & Sunshine HoursDaylight hours are in an increasing trend in February, but relatively short: they are about 10.4 hours and 11.3 hours, respectively, at the beginning and the end of the month. Since the sun sets quite early at around 17:29-17:52, getting up early is advised if you want to have a rich trip. Alternatively, you can extend your time on the daily tour by arranging some night visits. Anyway, the night views of Shanghai are awesome and the Bund is always on the top list. 
Generally, rainy and overcast moments occupy many hours of the daytime, and the sunshine hours are only 4 on average per day. The good news is that the sunshine is soft at this time, and you can enjoy outings without any sun-protection measures.
Averages for Shanghai Weather in February
Temperature: 6°C / 43°F
High Temperature: 8°C / 46°F
Low Temperature: 2°C / 36°F
Humidity: 71%
Rainfall: 60 mm
Rainy Days: 12 days
Sunrise: 06:22 ~ 06:47
Sunset: 17:29 ~ 17:52

What to Wear in Shanghai in February? Tops: Given the changeable climate of Shanghai in February, clothes of various thicknesses are needed. In detail, you are recommended to bring long-sleeved T-shirts and shirts; hoodies and knitwear; thick jackets like padded leather jackets and wool coats; and thin down jackets. 
On most daytime hours, long-sleeved shirts, hoodies, plus padded leather jackets; or long-sleeved T-shirts, knitwear, plus wool coats are suitable and comfortable to wear. During the daytime hours on some quite warm days, the outermost layer may need to be taken off. Then, during the nighttime hours, down jackets are generally necessary.
Bottoms: For pants, thick jeans and sweatpants are both suitable choices. Long johns are useful for activities like taking the Huangpu River cruise at night. The shoes you bring should be warm and comfortable for walking, so you can bring various thick flats and sneakers. 
Others: Always take rain gear with you in case it rains. Hats and scarves are better to be packed.
What Is Shanghai Like in February?
In 2027, both the Chinese New Year and the Lantern Festival will fall in February. At this time, Shanghai finds itself enveloped in the lively festive atmosphere. In addition, some flowers begin to bloom. 
1. Yu Garden
Within the classical Garden, flowers like daffodils and plum blossoms compete to bloom. Outside the Garden, numerous large-scale lanterns themed around the Chinese New Year are visible. During the Lantern Festival period, activities like lantern riddle guessing and folk performances will enrich your itinerary. Lightened Yuyuan Bazaar Yu Garden Lantern Festival 
2. Lujiazui & The Bund
Beyond the ever-impressive “World Architecture Expo” and the Oriental Pearl Tower, you can admire romantic violets blooming along the Bund in February. This month, visiting this area at night offers not only stunning cityscapes but also the chance to witness spectacular iron flower performances against the dazzling backdrop of the Oriental Pearl Tower.
3. Zhujiajiao Water Town
Red lanterns lined the bridges and rivers of the Water Town. Besides, folk markets and folk performances will deliver you some special festival experiences.
4. Shanghai Disney Resort
Castles and parks adorned with festival decorations, and New Year-themed parades and exclusive holiday performances can be admired.
Is February Crowded for a Visit?
That depends on the specific dates. 
Generally speaking, most of February is quiet with fewer tourists due to the somewhat cold weather of Shanghai. So, you will not feel crowded in most attractions, and spend a bit less on hotels.  Quiet Shanghai in February 
However, you should note that the period of the Chinese New Year holiday is when Shanghai is full of domestic visitors, which is usually in January or February. At that time, famous attractions like the Yu Garden, Nanjing Road, the Bund, etc., are quite crowded; long lines form for each item in Shanghai Disneyland Park; and hotels surge in their prices… In 2027, the holiday will fall from February 4 to 12. 
Tips for Visiting Shanghai in February
1. Try to avoid visiting Shanghai during the Chinese New Year holiday. On the one hand, the city will be crowded, and hotels will be quite expensive. On the other hand, some restaurants and malls will close temporarily. Don’t worry that you will miss the festival atmosphere - the decorations mentioned above will be available for more than one month.
2. Book your hotels and tickets for attractions in advance, after all, Shanghai is quite a popular tourist destination both at home and abroad.

Shanghai Weather in March
 In March, spring weather warms up the whole city of Shanghai. Some drizzles fall, bringing the vibrant spring picture: the air is fresh and clean, trees like willows bud, flowers like cherry blossoms and tulips gradually bloom… Nice weather and bright spring scenery make March a definitely good month to visit Shanghai.
TemperatureAn overall increasing trend can be noticed throughout March. In the first half of the month, still a little cold days with the daily high and low of around 10-15 degrees Celsius (50-59 degrees Fahrenheit) and 5-10°C (41-50°F), respectively, are more common. In the second half month, warm days, which enjoy daytime temperature of around 15-25°C (59-77°F) and nighttime temperature of 10-15°C (50-59°F), show up more frequently.  Yu Garden in Cold March 
However, you cannot decide what to pack for your trip based only on the above overall temperature picture: instability is also an obvious feature of the temperature of Shanghai in March that cannot be overlooked. On the one hand, the temperature gap between day and night can be quite large, which may be over 15°C (27°F) sometimes. For instance, on March 2, 2025, the daytime was warm or even a bit hot at around 28°C (82°F), while the nighttime brought cold air with the temperature of only 10°C (50°F). On the other hand, temperature differences between two consecutive days can also be big, which are demonstrated by sudden temperature drops or rises of around 5-15°C (9-27°F).
Precipitation & HumidityAbout 14 rainy days show up in March on average, which is relatively frequent, but the average monthly precipitation is not high at only 84 mm. This indicates that drizzle is the main type of rain this month. What is also favorable for your trip is that drizzles usually stop quickly, followed by gentle sunshine. 
Shanghai suffers from wet and damp air in March, and the humidity is about 70% on average. You will feel even colder when the temperature is low, due to the high humidity.
 The Bund on Sunny Days Clear Sky in March  
Daylight Hours & Sunshine HoursMarch in Shanghai gets gradually extending daytime from about 11.3 to 12.3 hours, so you don’t need to worry that you cannot gain enough daylight for walking around, and just slow down and have a leisurely trip, especially in the second half of the month. Besides, with relatively early sunset time at 17:51-18:12, you can enjoy illuminated night views early.
Plenty of sunshine guarantees good visibility and light conditions for outdoor visiting and photographing: sunshine hours per day average about 5 hours this month. During the midday hours of sunny days, when the UV index can reach 7, sun-protection measures are essential, especially for those having sensitive skin. 
Averages for Shanghai Weather in March
Temperature: 9°C / 48°F
High Temperature: 13°C / 55°F
Low Temperature: 5°C / 41°F
Humidity: 70%
Rainfall: 84 mm
Rainy Days: 14 days
Sunrise: 05:45 ~ 06:21
Sunset: 17:53 ~ 18:13
Air Quality in March
Average AQI:63
One of the Best Months to Visit ShanghaiMarch is considered one of the best months to visit Shanghai and trips to the Bund, the Yu Garden, the Nanjing Road, etc., will all reward you with perfect experiences:
1. Temperature-wise, Shanghai is gradually getting rid of the damp and chilly weather and becoming warmer and warmer, while sudden temperature drops take place only occasionally.
2. Rain, though a bit frequently, is usually light and short, guaranteeing plenty of sunshine.
3. The visitor volume is moderate this month, so you can book nice hotel rooms at budget-friendly prices and visit attractions at a leisurely pace without waiting in lines for a long period.
4. In March, Shanghai is ablaze with vibrant spring colors, as bright flowers bloom everywhere.  Disneyland Park Full of Flowers in March  
What to Wear in Shanghai in March 2027? Clothes: The weather of Shanghai in March is changeable, so you need to prepare clothes of different thicknesses. On most days in the first half of the month, and on some days in the second half of the month when Shanghai is hit by cold air, you should wear hoodies, thick sweatpants, and down jackets or wool coats. On most days in the second half month, you can change the down jackets or wool coats into 3-in-1 jackets or windbreakers. Sometimes, when the daytime temperature is over 25°C (77°F), even a trench coat or an outer layer of a 3-in-1 jacket alone is enough.
Shoes: Choose a pair of comfortable and relatively thick sneakers, walking shoes, or boots.
Others: 
1. Never forget to bring an umbrella with you when traveling to Shanghai in March.
2. Sun-protection items like sunglasses, hats, and sunscreen are better to prepare.
3. People who are allergic to pollen are advised to wear masks
Tips for Visiting Shanghai in March1. As mentioned above, March will not see very high visitor flow in Shanghai, and the Shanghai Disneyland Park also welcomes its rare slack season. You will indeed have a smoother trip that requires a relatively short time to queue; however, you should know that due to the decline in visitor numbers, the Park will close early, and the number of fireworks shows and parade performances will be reduced. If you plan to visit it this month, please check the related information in advance.
2. Try to arrange your travel on weekdays. In this month of flower blooming, weekends are the time for the locals to spring out, indicating that parks and public transportation will be crowded.
3. The climate of Shanghai in March is quite changeable, making it important to check the weather forecast from time to time. Shanghai Spring View 
4. Want to see flowers to feel the spring? Yu Garden provides pink cherry blossoms and white magnolias, and the area around the Oriental Pearl Tower has white magnolias and tulips to see. Or, if time permits, Gu Village Park, boasting 16,000 trees and a lively cherry blossom festival, and Jing’an Sculpture Park in the city center, with large-scale cherry blossoms and tulips, are recommended destinations to visit.

Shanghai Weather in April
 April is definitely one of the best choices for those who are planning to visit Shanghai. The daytime is warm and pleasant and the nighttime is cool. Sunny moments are common and only some short-term drizzles occur from time to time. As for the natural scenery, the color of spring has splashed every inch of the city and all things are reinvigorated.
Warm Daytime and Cool NighttimeApril, a spring month, boasts quite warm and comfortable daytime. The first a few days may still see the daily high of 15-20 degrees Celsius (59-68 degrees Fahrenheit), but since then, the daily high temperature climbs and ranges from around 20°C (68°F) to 27°C (81°F). Occasionally, the city may even experience a hot midday with the high temperature of 30-33°C (86-91°F).
The daily temperature gap is large in Shanghai in April, and it is usually over 10°C (18°F). More specifically, the daily low is mainly in the range of 10-15°C (50-59°F), and occasionally reaches beyond 15°C (59°F) on the last several days of this month. Therefore, on most nights in Shanghai in April, you will still feel a distinct chill in the air. Cozy Daytime of April  
Frequent but Light and Short-duration RainThe overall precipitation is at a moderate level of 130 mm on average in April. The number of rainy days, which is 15 on average, is one of the largest throughout the year. 
However, actually, the rain won’t produce much inconvenience for your tour. According to the historical records, the rain this month is usually light in intensity and short in duration.
As for the humidity, it averages 69% this month, and the air is a bit damp. Thanks to the pleasant temperature, the relatively high humidity will not cause an uncomfortable feeling. Sunny View of Shanghai in April  
Long Daylight Hours & Strong UV RaysThe early sunrise at around 05:11-05:43 and late sunset at 18:13-18:33 contribute to another favorable weather condition for traveling around: long daytime. In general, the daylight hours stretch from 12.3 to 13.2 from the beginning to the end of the month. There is no need to rush during the sightseeing, even if you have a relatively packed schedule. 
Sunshine hours average 5 this month. You should be especially careful about the strong sunlight. At midday, the UV index can reach as high as 9, and if you are exposed to this sun light for a long time without taking protection measures, your skin may get sunburned easily.

Temperature: 15°C / 59°F
High Temperature: 19°C / 66°F
Low Temperature: 11°C / 52°F

Rainfall: 103 mm

Air Quality in April
Average AQI: 52
What to Pack When Visiting Shanghai in April? Clothes: For the warm daytime, outfits like long-sleeved T-shirts plus sweatpants, short-sleeved T-shirts and shirts plus jeans, and long-sleeved dresses plus thin leggings are all suitable. On some sunny midday hours in late April, even T-shirts plus shorts or skirts are OK to wear. With huge temperature differences between day and night, after sunset, trench coats, leather jackets, or denim jackets are needed.
Shoes: Sneakers, canvas shoes, and loafers are all good choices, as long as they are comfortable enough.
Others: 
1. During sunny daytime, sun-protection items, including sunglasses, hats, and sunscreen, are essential.
2. An umbrella should be put into your bag for possible rain.
3. This month is the pollen season, and those with rhinitis are recommended to prepare some masks.
What to See When Visiting Shanghai in April?In warm April with many sunny hours, you will find it a very pleasant experience whether you are visiting the Yu Garden to admire the traditional Chinese garden architecture, heading to the Bund to take in the night views, or strolling down Nanjing Road to experience the bustling view of Shanghai. In addition, following special highlights in April may deliver you more choices and a richer experience. Dazzling Night View  
1. Lively Festivals(1) Longhua Temple Fair
Each year, the temple fair is held on the 3rd day of the 3rd lunar month, which is usually in April. During the temple fair, folk performances can be admired, souvenirs can be bought in the cultural and creative products market, and delicious local food can be tasted. In 2027, it will take place on April 9 of the Gregorian calendar.
(2) Formula 1 Chinese Grand Prix
It has been held at the Shanghai International Circuit since 2004 and is a key Asian stop on the F1 calendar. It is typically held in April each year. If you’re a motorsports fan, this is definitely an event you won’t want to miss.
2. Vibrant Spring ViewIn April, Shanghai looks like a giant garden. You will find charming spring views in Yu Garden, Zhujiajiao Water Town, Century Park, the Shanghai Botanical Garden, People’s Park, Jing’an Sculpture Park, etc., which are all bursting with colorful flowers and lush green trees. 
 Street View of Shanghai in April Spring View of the Yu Garden 
Is Shanghai Crowded in April?April indeed sees a growing number of visitors due to the overall pleasant weather of Shanghai and beautiful scenery. Accordingly, famous attractions like the Yuyuan Garden and the Bund will be a little crowded, and hotel prices will grow by much.
Pay special attention to the fact that the first and last a few days of the month will be much more crowded than usual: The Qingming Festival falls on April 4 or 5, and a three-day public holiday is given; and at the end of April, many Chinese will be arriving in Shanghai to start their May Day holiday.
Tips for Shanghai Trips in April1. For trips to Shanghai this month with many tourists, early booking, for both attractions and hotels, is the top priority, especially if your traveling dates are in early or late April, two periods that are actually advised to avoid. 
2. The climate of Shanghai in April is kind of changeable, so remember to check the weather forecast from time to time. On rainy days, you are advised to adjust your itinerary flexibly and add some indoor activities like visiting the Shanghai Museum and the Shanghai Science and Technology Museum, and hang around in malls.
