Shanghai Weather in May
 Shanghai weather in May is warm overall, usually with the daily high temperature above 25°C (77°F). Drizzles fall from time to time, but usually stop quickly, guaranteeing long enough sunshine hours for you to travel around. Scenery-wise, Shanghai in May is vibrant, colorful, and fragrant with new plants and blooming flowers. Considering all of these, May is absolutely one of the best months to visit Shanghai.
Temperature
In the first half of May, Shanghai features warm and cozy daytime and cool nighttime: the daily high temperature is mainly in the range of 20-27 degrees Celsius (68-81 degrees Fahrenheit), and the daily low fluctuates between 15°C (59°F) and 20°C (68°F). 
In the second half of the month, the temperature rises. On most days, the daytime is warm or even a bit hot at 25-32°C (86-91°F), and the nighttime turns relatively warm with the temperature above 20°C (68°F). Usually, at the end of May, Shanghai enters summer, and it’s not rare that the highest temperature of a day reaches around 35°C (95°F).
There are two other things that you should pay attention to: First, rain may bring sudden temperature drops, so sometimes, you may wear a T-shirt alone during the midday hours on a day and need to put on a denim jacket during the same time period of the next day. Second, temperature can vary a lot from day to night, usually 7-10°C (18°F). Warm Shanghai in May  
Rainfall & Humidity
Shanghai in May doesn’t receive much rainfall, which averages about 115 mm. It is scattered over 15 rainy days on average, meaning that the possibility of encountering rain during your trip is a bit high. Fortunately, the rain mainly falls in the form of soft drizzles or quickly stopping showers, affecting your trip only slightly.
The relatively high humidity, 71% on average, may make you feel a bit stuffy during the midday hours in late May. The Bund in Sunny May  
Daylight Hours & Sunshine Hours
Daytime is about 13-14 hours long this month, quite enough to have a rich as well as leisurely trip. For those who get into the habit of getting up early, you have the chance to explore the quiet aspect of this metropolis as sunrise time is as early as 04:51-05:10. Besides, the sunset time is not very late, at around 18:33-18:53, indicating that you can admire the night view and experience the nightlife relatively early, and thus go back to the hotels and have a rest not too late. 
Since there are rarely long-lasting rains, the sunshine hours reach around 6 per day on average, and you can enjoy bright sunshine most of the time during your tour. However, when enjoying the sunshine, do not ignore making necessary sun-protection measures - the UV rays are quite strong this month with the maximum UV index of 10.
Averages for Shanghai Weather in May
Temperature: 20°C / 68°F
High Temperature: 24°C / 75°F
Low Temperature: 16°C / 61°F
Humidity: 71%
Rainfall: 115 mm
Rainy Days: 15 days
Sunrise: 04:51 ~ 05:10
Sunset: 18:33 ~ 18:53
Air Quality in May
Average AQI:52
What to Pack When Visiting Shanghai in May? Clothes: Generally speaking, the warm climate of Shanghai in the daytime of May allows summer clothes. So, males can bring short-sleeve T-shirts, shorts, and thin long pants; while females can additionally pack dresses and skirts. Because of the temperature gap between day and night, thin jackets or long-sleeve shirts are needed.
Shoes: Comfortable and breathable sneakers and flats are the first choice.
Accessories: To protect yourself from the rain and the sunshine, a parasol, sunglasses, sunhats, and sun-blocking cream are recommended to bring.
Crowds and Scenery of Shanghai in MayCrowds:
Each May 1-5, the Chinese have a five-day public holiday and may travel around to relax. Shanghai, one of the most popular tourist destinations in China, attracts numerous visitors during this period. If you travel to Shanghai at that time, you will see numerous visitors in famous attractions like the Bund and the Yu Garden, need to wait in endless queues to experience programs in Shanghai Disneyland Park, and have to spend much more for hotels than usual… Crowded Nanjing Road in Early May 
After the holiday, Shanghai becomes quieter, but various attractions still receive many visitors - after all, May is a month with quite favorable and comfortable weather conditions. Hotels also become a bit cheaper compared with the first a few days of the month.
Scenery:
In May, Shanghai is a picturesque place with vibrant blooms and lush greenery. Visiting Shanghai at this time allows you to experience both the bustling energy of this metropolis at places like the Bund and the vitality of the countryside in its various parks. In addition, flower shows are held in downtown areas like Huangpu Xintiandi and Qiantan, offering vibrant and stunning views well worth a visit. Lush View of the Yu Garden  
Tips and Recommendations for Shanghai Trips in May 20271. As mentioned above, Shanghai during the period from May 1 to 5 will be very crowded, so it is highly recommended to avoid this time. If you fail to do so, you need to take the following measures to make the trip go more smoothly.
(1) Choose and book hotels that you are satisfied with in advance. 
(2) Arrange visits for popular attractions in the early morning to avoid main crowds. For instance, if you arrive at and begin to visit the Yu Garden at around 09:00, the time that the Garden just opens, you will enjoy a relatively quiet scene.

On sunny days, it is warm and of good visibility, while on rainy days, it is cool but not cold, and you have a chance to see the Town showing a hazy and misty scene.  Zhujiajiao Water Town in May

Shanghai Weather in June
 June belongs to the summer, and Shanghai enters its plum rainy season in the middle of the month, so the weather features high temperature, high rainfall, and high humidity. If you can accept the a bit unfavorable weather of Shanghai during this month, you will be rewarded with a relatively quiet city bursting with greenery and a limited-time sea of flowers.
Rainy Season with High Rainfall and HumidityAround mid-June each year, Shanghai enters the plum rainy season, featuring frequent overcast and rainy weather. On average, this month sees the highest precipitation of the year, at 159 mm, and rainy days account for nearly half of the month. To make matters worse, the month has both persistent drizzles and sudden downpours, both of which may disrupt your outdoor plans and cause significant inconvenience.
Another characteristic of the plum rainy season is high humidity. In June, Shanghai’s average humidity is 79%, also the highest of the year, which undoubtedly makes the air feel damp and stifling. Traveling to Shanghai this month, you will find that the tissues on the table of hotels are almost always damp, and laundry takes 4-5 days or more to dry. Gloomy Shanghai in June  
High TemperatureJune marks the beginning of summer in Shanghai. While temperatures are relatively high, the frequent rainfall keeps them from becoming excessively high. On most cloudy or rainy days, high temperatures in Shanghai hover around 25-30 degrees Celsius (77-86 degrees Fahrenheit), while low temperatures are around 20°C (68°F). On most sunny days, daily highs typically range from 30 to 35°C (86-95°F), and the daily lows are around 23-25°C (73-77°F). At times, especially toward the end of the month, the daily highs can reach around 36-38°C (97-100°F).
When the temperatures rise above 35°C (95°F), there is no doubt that outdoor activities will become quite challenging. However, you should know that in June, you will not feel very cozy even on days with daily highs of around 30-35°C (86-95°F): the high humidity makes the apparent temperature much higher and creates a sticky sensation.  Hot June on Cloudy Day  
Daylight Hours & Sunshine HoursThe day turns bright quite early at 04:51-04:53 this month, and becomes dark at 18:53-19:02. As a result, Shanghai gains quite long daylight hours of over 14 hours. However, since it’s in the rainy season, the sunlight is usually blocked by clouds, and it is common to encounter overcast weather all day long. As a result, the sunshine hours are only 4-5 hours per day on average.
However, once the sun is shining, you need to take some measures to protect your skin, because the UV index can reach 11 this month.
Averages for Shanghai Weather in June
Temperature: 24°C / 75°F
High Temperature: 27°C / 81°F
Low Temperature: 20°C / 68°F
Humidity: 79%
Rainfall: 159mm
Rainy Days:15 days
Sunrise: 04:51 ~ 04:53
Sunset: 18:53 ~ 19:02
Air Quality in June
Average AQI: 37
Is June a Good Time to Visit Shanghai?It depends on the dates that you choose to travel.
Generally speaking, the scenery of Shanghai is beautiful and worth-visiting whole month. However, weather-wise, the temperature in the first half of June is slightly lower than that in the second half, and the rain usually falls not very frequently in the first half since the rainy season has not yet come. So, you can have a not-bad travel experience if you visit Shanghai during the first half of June. 
What to Pack When Visiting Shanghai in June?  Clothes: To stay comfortable in the damp and hot daytime, summer clothes as thin and breathable as possible are recommended to bring. For example, loose-fit and quick-dry tank tops, T-shirts, shorts, skirts, dresses, and thin long pants are good choices. Another piece of advice is to choose light-colored clothes that absorb less heat than dark-colored ones. Some nights may be a bit cool, so consider bringing shirts or thin jackets, which can also block the sunshine during the sunny daytime.
 Shoes: The shoes you pack should be both comfortable for walking and breathable, so try to search your shoe cabinet for cozy sandals, canvas shoes, and sneakers with breathable mesh uppers. 
 Others:
1. To prevent the harm of strong UV rays, sunglasses, sunhats, and sunscreen are needed to bring.
2. Rain is quite common in Shanghai in June, so always take an umbrella with you. Besides, you are recommended to put some travel-sized tissues in your bag for timely use.
3. With hot and humid environment, mosquitoes are rampant this month, making insect repellent sprays and stickers important.
What Does Shanghai Look Like in June?
1. June Scenery of Classic Attractions(1) The Bund: On a sunny day, the significant skyscrapers are clearly visible, with the background of blue and clear sky. On rainy days with mist, the skyline becomes hazy, and the Bund is in a quiet and unique atmosphere. From 19:00 to 23:00, a scene of dazzling lights can be seen.
(2) Zhujiajiao / Yu Garden: They are lush and green all around. In the rainy season, shrouded in misty rain, these sites take on an even more rustic and elegant charm, resembling a tranquil and poetic painting slowly unfolding before your eyes. Stunning Night View of the Bund  
2. Lively Activities(1) Activities for Dragon Boat Festival: In 2027, the Dragon Boat Festival falls on June 9. Various celebratory events will be held throughout Shanghai. For example, Zhujiajiao Water Town will feature folk performances, dragon boat races, and other Dragon Boat Festival-themed exhibitions. Of course, you can also sample zongzi, the food for the festival specially. In addition to Zhujiajiao, Yu Garden, Old City God Temple, and some malls will also host Dragon Boat Festival markets during this period.
(2) In 2027, June 16 marks the 11th anniversary of Shanghai Disney Resort. Special events will be held on that day.
Tips for Shanghai Trips in June Zhujiajiao Water Town in Rain 1. In June, Shanghai generally sees moderate visitor traffic. However, the Dragon Boat Festival holiday falling on June 19-21 in 2026 is an exception. During this short holiday, there will be a surge in domestic visitors to Shanghai, and popular attractions such as the Bund, Nanjing Road, and Shanghai Disneyland Park will experience peak crowds. So, early booking is needed if you plan to visit Shanghai during this period.
2. The sun rises early, so consider heading out early each day to explore the city, as the mornings are generally cooler. Try to avoid scheduling outdoor activities for the hottest 12:00-14:00 to prevent discomfort or even heatstroke.
3. When traveling to Shanghai in rainy June, be sure to check the weather forecast regularly. You can visit popular outdoor attractions on both sunny and drizzly days - on drizzly days, places like the Yu Garden, Zhujiajiao, and the Bund offer a different yet still beautiful scenery. If it rains heavily, visiting museums or shopping malls or similar indoor places will be a more comfortable option.

Shanghai Weather in July
 The weather of Shanghai in July is far from ideal. Temperatures typically hover above 30°C (86°F) during the daytime and often exceed 35°C (95°F), leading to quite hot air. As for precipitation, early July still belongs to the plum rainy season, and typhoon may occur in later month, making the weather of Shanghai unpredictable and rainy. But Shanghai is vibrant and lively in July, with lush and green trees and beautiful flowers in full blossom like the lotus flowers. Lush and Beautiful Zhujiajiao in July  
RainfallOverall, there is an average of approximately 135 mm of rainfall and 12 rainy days in Shanghai in July. The precipitation patterns are somewhat complex:
  Rainy View of Zhujiajiao Water Town In early July, Shanghai is still in the plum rainy season. During this period, the city may experience several consecutive days of overcast and rainy weather, with the possibility of heavy or even torrential downpours.
Around July 10 each year, the rainy season ends. Then, in mid-July, precipitation generally takes the form of thunderstorms that come and go quickly. At the same time, there are more sunny periods compared to early July.
By late July, the typhoon season arrives, and Shanghai may be hit by a typhoon, although the probability is not very high. When not affected by typhoons, rainfall is still primarily in the form of thunderstorms with limited influence on your sightseeing. However, when affected by typhoons, persistent heavy or even violent rain accompanied by strong winds may occur. Luckily, it usually affects people’s life for only 1-2 days. 
TemperatureTraveling to Shanghai in July means that you are going to experience the hottest weather of Shanghai throughout the year.
This month, the daytime temperature is quite high at a range of around 30-38 degrees Celsius (86-100 degrees Fahrenheit), and in some years, the extreme high temperature can even reach 40°C (104°F). According to the historical data, in each July, there are about 7-15 days when the daily high is over 35°C (95°F). What’s worse, the weather of Shanghai features high humidity that averages 76% this month, leading to obviously muggy feelings: just 10 to 20 minutes of outdoor activities during the daytime will have you sweating buckets. 
With a daily low of about 26-30°C (79-86°F), nighttime is OK and a bit cozier to roam around compared with the daytime, though you will also not feel cool. Visitors in the Yu Garden in Hot July  
Daylight Hours & Sunshine HoursThe sun rises at around 4:54-5:10 and doesn’t set until around 18:50-19:02. Therefore, the daytime is very long at about 14 hours on average. So, feel free to skip some of the hottest times during the day to ensure a better travel experience without worrying that the available time is not enough.
Sunlight hours last for about 7 per day on average. During these hours, the sunshine is often very intense: the UV index frequently reaches as high as 11.
Averages for Shanghai Weather in July
Temperature: 28°C / 82°F
High Temperature: 32°C / 90°F
Low Temperature: 25°C / 77°F
Humidity: 76%
Rainfall: 135 mm
Rainy Days: 12 days
Sunrise: 04:54 ~ 05:10
Sunset: 18:50 ~ 19:02
Air Quality in July
Average AQI: 42
Is July a Good Time to Visit Shanghai?Not really, even though Shanghai in July is surrounded by lush greenery and beautiful flowers.
First of all, Shanghai is sticky and rainy in July. During your trip, you can expect either sunny but muggy weather with scorching sun or slightly cooler weather with light to heavy rain. Not to mention, if you travel to Shanghai in late July, there’s a possibility you will be stuck in your hotel because of a typhoon.
Another piece of bad news is that July is the time when Chinese students are on summer vacation. So, it’s not weird at all if you find that the prices for hotels and Shanghai Disneyland Park become extremely high and popular attractions like the Bund and the Yu Garden are packed with family groups. Crowded Nanjing Road in July 
Then, if this is your only available time, is there any way to make the experience a little better? Of course:
Pack Proper Clothes and Items  Clothes: The clothes you pack for your Shanghai trips in July are better to be thin, air-permeable, light-colored, and quick-dry. Specifically, you can bring cool tank tops, T-shirts, shorts, thin long pants, and dresses. Don’t forget to prepare one or two thin jackets or shirts to deal with the coolness in malls and on the metro with effective air conditioners. Besides, considering that the weather is humid and clothes don’t dry easily, you are recommended to bring more for timely change.
 Shoes: Flats like canvas shoes, sneakers, and sandals that can keep you cool and comfortable are all OK. Be sure to bring some breathable socks. 
 Other Items:
1. Always bring an umbrella with you to cope with the changing climate of Shanghai in July. 
2. Sun protection is a top priority, so be sure to bring high-SPF sunscreen, sunglasses, and sun hats.
3. To stay cool and prevent heatstroke, carry wet tissues and a water bottle with you at all times.
4. Insect repellent and anti-itch cream are essential in damp and hot July when mosquitoes are rampant.
Plan Your Itinerary in Advance and Based on the Weather Conditions 
1. How to Have a Better Experience in this Crowded MonthFirst, be sure to make reservations in advance - whether for hotels or tickets to popular attractions like the Shanghai Museum and Disneyland Park. Otherwise, you might miss out on attractions you’re interested in or end up spending more. Second, you are recommended to choose a hotel near a subway station and get up early on the days of your trip. That way, you can start your sightseeing as early as possible and avoid the main crowds. For example, you are advised to arrive at the Yu Garden right when it opens. This period is also relatively cooler and comfortable for outdoor activities. Quieter Yu Garden in Early Morning  
2. How to Survive the High TemperatureArrange some indoor attractions with air conditioning for the hottest period from 12:00 to 14:00, when the sunshine is also at its strongest. Specifically, the best way to spend this time is to visit museums, art galleries, shopping malls, or other indoor venues, or to stay at your hotel and rest.
Then, schedule more evening tours to make up for the time lost during the midday: Shanghai boasts rich nighttime activities for you to choose from. For example, you can head to the Bund to enjoy the glittering night views, take a night cruise on the Huangpu River, overlook the night views of the city at the highest point of the Oriental Pearl Tower, walk around in Nanjing Road, and visit the Yuyuan Bazaar. Night Cruise on the Huangpu River  
3. Tips on Visiting Shanghai in Rainy JulyKeeping an eye on the weather forecast is quite important during your Shanghai tour in July 2027.
If there will be heavy rain or downpours, you are recommended to have a backup plan, like visiting indoor attractions and shopping malls. If the rain tends to be brief, you can just find a cafe to sit down when it comes, take a short break, and enjoy the quiet charm of Shanghai in the rain before continuing your trip.

Shanghai Weather in August
 With high temperature and humidity, the weather of Shanghai in August is unbearably sweltering. In terms of rainfall, the city suffers both brief showers and long-duration and heavy rains brought by the typhoon this month. Despite the unfavorable weather, August is a high travel season because it is the summer holiday in China. 
TemperatureAugust is a summer month in Shanghai, and the defining characteristic of the weather is extremely hot.
Throughout the month, daytime temperature hovers around 35 degrees Celsius (95 degrees Fahrenheit), with the maximum value typically reaching 38-40°C (100-104°F). To make matters worse, the humidity in Shanghai this month stands at 77%, making the air feel even more stifling: sometimes, the weather forecast says a daytime high of around 36-37°C (97-99°F), but in reality, the heat index can feel like around 40°C (104°F). Nighttime temperature generally ranges from 25 to 30°C (77-86°F), which is still far from cool.
In some years, the weather of last a few days of the month gets slightly cooler, with daily highs and lows around 27-33°C (81-91°F) and 23-26°C (73-79°F), respectively.  People Visiting the Yu Garden in Hot August  
RainfallThe rainfall of Shanghai in August remains at a relatively high level of 136 mm on average. During the averagely 11 rainy days, brief showers are more common, which tend to have less influence on your trips. 
What needs your special attention is that Shanghai may suffer typhoons in August. Typhoons may make direct landfall in Shanghai or pass by very closely. Although infrequently, when they do, they bring long-term heavy rain and strong winds, leading to widespread flight cancellations and the closure of tourist attractions. One or two times, Shanghai may be affected by the outer bands of a typhoon this month. During such times, while winds and rain may come and go intermittently, they will not be very strong and you can still go out and visit indoor attractions. Sunny View of the Bund  
Daylight Hours & Sunshine HoursFrom the beginning to the end of the month, the sunrise time changes from 05:11 to 05:30, and the sunset time changes from 18:50 to 18:19. Accordingly, daylight hours in Shanghai gradually shorten in August, from 13.1 to 12.4. Luckily, they are still long enough for daily exploration, but remember to arrange some indoor visits for the sticky midday hours from 12:00 to 14:00.
The highest UV index reaches 11 this month, signifying that the sunshine is pretty intense. Besides, the sunshine hours reach around 8 per day on average. So, during your Shanghai trips in August, you have a high chance of seeing beautiful Shanghai under bright sunshine and blue and clear sky, but you need to take sun-protection measures.

Temperature: 28°C / 82°F
High Temperature: 32°C / 90°F
Low Temperature: 25°C / 77°F
Humidity: 77%
Rainfall: 136 mm
Rainy Days: 11 days
Sunrise: 05:11 ~ 05:30
Sunset: 18:19 ~ 18:50
Air Quality in August
Average AQI: 36
What to Bring to Survive in Hot and Rainy August? Clothes: There’s no doubt that you need to pack summer clothing such as sleeveless or short-sleeved T-shirts, shorts, and dresses to help you stay cool in the stuffy and hot climate of Shanghai. In addition to this, there are a few other things you should keep in mind:
1. First, it’s best to choose lightweight and breathable ones, such as those made of cotton, linen, or silk. 
2. Second, opt for light-colored clothing, as black ones absorb heat and will make you feel even hotter. 
3. Third, it’s best to pack several sets, since when temperatures reach around 35°C (95°F), your clothes can easily become soaked with sweat. 
4. Fourth, bring a light jacket like a sun-protection jacket in case feeling cold in air-conditioned places. 
Shoes: Choose one or two pairs among comfortable sandals, lightweight mesh sneakers, and slip-on canvas shoes.
Accessories:
1. High-SPF sunscreen, hats, and sunglasses are recommended to protect you against the strong UV rays. An all-weather umbrella is useful on both rainy and sunny days.
2. Consider bringing a portable fan, wet wipes, and a water bottle to help you stay comfortable in the blazing sun.
3. Insect repellent is needed in muggy August. 
Crowds of Shanghai in AugustAugust marks China’s summer vacation, and Shanghai, as a major international metropolis, attracts many family groups, making it even more crowded than usual. Whether you visit Disneyland Park, museums, or the Yu Garden during the daytime or head to the Bund at nighttime, you will find that you are surrounded by throngs of tourists. Additionally, hotel rates will be significantly higher than usual. Crowded Disneyland Park 
Since the summer vacation ends in early September, the number of tourists drops significantly by the end of August.
Tips for Traveling to Shanghai in August 20271. If possible, arrange your trip for late August, when the summer holiday crowds have dispersed and the weather may turn a little bit cooler.
2. Try to avoid weekends and book hotels and tickets for attractions as soon as possible.
3. Early morning and evening are the coolest periods of the day in August, so you are recommended to take full use of them to do some outdoor visits. As for the hottest 12:00-14:00, you’d better do some indoor visits, like exploring the Shanghai Museum. Our Guests at the Shanghai Museum 
4. Pay close attention to the weather forecast to keep informed about whether there is a typhoon during your stay. If there is, be sure to make adjustments promptly.
5. Since there are so many tourists in Shanghai during the summer holiday, some attractions may extend their opening hours. For instance, in 2025, the Shanghai Museum opened some exhibition halls 24 hours from August 11 to 17, and the Shanghai Natural History Museum extended its closing time to 20:00 for the entire month. Besides, Disneyland Park may open till 22:00 on some days in August.

Shanghai Weather in September
 From early to late September, Shanghai weather transitions from stuffy to a bit cool. As for rainfall, showers occur frequently but don’t significantly impact travel; besides, there is a relatively high probability of a typhoon striking, especially around the middle of the month. It may not be a perfect time to visit Shanghai. That said, September is a rare time when Shanghai isn’t overly crowded, except around the Mid-Autumn Festival. Zhujiajiao View in September  
Hot First Half Month and Cooler Second HalfTraveling to Shanghai in the first half of September, you will basically have hot and not very comfortable experiences during your outdoor visits, especially in the daytime. Generally speaking, Shanghai is still in summer at this time, and the daily high temperature is mainly in the range of 30-35 degrees Celsius (86-95 degrees Fahrenheit) and reaches 36-38°C (97-100°F) occasionally. On top of that, the humid air makes the weather muggy. Nighttime tours are indeed a little more comfortable than daytime ones, but don’t expect the weather to turn cool: the daily low is at 25-28°C (68-82°F), and on sunny days, the temperature is still high at around 30°C (86°F) at 21:00.
Entering the second half month, the temperature shows a downward trend. Most of the time, the daily high and low hovers around 30°C (86°F) and 23°C (73°F), respectively, indicating that you will no longer feel uncomfortably hot at that time. Note that exceptions may exist, for instance, in 2025, several days in late September still experienced hot daytime with the high temperature of 34-35°C (93-95°F). Visitors in Shanghai in Hot Early September  
Showers Fall Frequently, and Typhoon May OccurRain falls frequently this month in Shanghai: there are 13 rainy days on average. Fortunately, not all of them will influence your trip.
Most of the time, the rain comes and stops quickly and usually in the afternoon, though sometimes heavy. In other words, when encountering rain during your tour this month, you can head to a cafe to take shelter from the rain. Then, maybe 30 minutes later, the sun will reappear, and you can continue your outdoor visit. Moreover, this kind of rain may bring temperature drops and bring a sense of coolness.
Note that the rainfalls caused by typhoons are different. Usually, the typhoon brings long-duration and high-intensity rain, during which you may need to stop your visit and stay in your hotel for safety. Over the past five years, Shanghai experienced three direct typhoon landfalls in September, and all in mid-month.
Daylight Hours & UV RaysDaylight hours are shortening from 12.5 to 11.5 this month. If you have a packed itinerary and want to have a rest at noon, you are recommended to get up early each day to gain enough visiting time, especially if your visiting dates are in late September.
UV index is high at 9 in Shanghai in September, making sun-protection measures necessary during the sunshine hours, which average 6 hours per day.
Averages for Shanghai Weather in September
Temperature: 24°C / 75°F
High Temperature: 27°C / 81°F
Low Temperature: 21°C / 70°F
Humidity: 74%
Rainfall: 152 mm
Rainy Days: 13 days
Sunrise: 05:30 ~ 05:47
Sunset: 17:41 ~ 17:17
Air Quality in September
Average AQI: 44
What to Wear in Shanghai in September？  Clothes: During the first half month, outfits like T-shirts plus skirts, short shirts plus shorts, and dresses are good choices. If you are worried about feeling cold in air-conditioned places like the metro, just bring a light jacket. 
Traveling to Shanghai during the second half month, especially the final days of the month, thin long pants are better choices than shorts. If girls want to wear skirts, longer ones are more recommended. Besides, add thin baseball jackets or long-sleeved shirts in the morning and evening. 
 Shoes: Sandals are OK in the first half month, while thin sneakers and casual shoes are more proper in the second half month.
 Others: Umbrella, sunglasses, and hats.
Crowds of Shanghai in SeptemberIn 2027, the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday will fall on September 15th, and then, three days later, the National Day holiday will begin. So, starting late September, you can expect extremely large crowds and quite high hotel prices in Shanghai. 
However, in the other time of September, Shanghai is in its shoulder season. You can have relatively quiet experiences in attractions like the Yu Garden and the Bund, wait in short lines for popular items in the Disneyland Park, and have a budget-friendly trip. Tranquil Yu Garden in September  
Tips for Traveling to Shanghai in SeptemberNo matter when you visit Shanghai, you will include some of the most popular attractions like the exquisite Yu Garden, the modern and dazzling Bund, the lively Nanjing Road, and the Shanghai Museum with a rich collection. However, you should plan your itinerary carefully to ensure a more comfortable and enjoyable trip.
Tips for Tours in Early SeptemberFor trips during this period, the biggest challenge will be the high heat. You are recommended to plan outdoor visits, such as exploring Yu Garden, in early morning. Then, during the hottest hours from 12:00-15:00, you can visit indoor attractions like the Shanghai Museum to keep cool. After that, when the heat gradually disappears, you can explore the Nanjing Road and go to the Bund to experience a beautiful sunset and the dazzling night view. Dazzling Night View  
Tips for Tours in Mid-SeptemberSpecial attention should be paid to the weather forecast to monitor whether there is a typhoon during your stay - this period is the peak season for typhoons. If there will be direct hit of a typhoon, you may want to advance or postpone your trip. So, you are advised to book hotels that can be canceled for free. If Shanghai is predicted to be affected only by the outer bands of a typhoon and you still plan to visit Shanghai during this period, you may want to add more indoor attractions to your travel list. 
Tips for Tours in Late SeptemberClimate of Shanghai turns better at this time: it is no longer very hot, and the peak typhoon season ends. So, you are prone to gaining a better travel experience during this period.
However, in 2027, if your travel days include September 15, the Mid-Autumn Festival Holiday, be sure to make related reservations in advance and be prepared for the higher travel expense. Besides, begin your daily trip early to avoid the main crowds. 
Travel Highlights of Shanghai in September
1. Shanghai Tourism FestivalIt is a major cultural and tourism event held in Shanghai every September. During the festival, numerous activities are organized. Among them, the most lively, spectacular, and unmissable event is the parade of performance troupes and floats that kicks off the festival on the Bund on opening day. In addition, every evening during the festival, the Huangpu River is illuminated by a series of dazzling light shows.
2. Mid-Autumn Festival EventsFor Chinese people, the Mid-Autumn Festival is an important time for family reunion, during which many attractions in Shanghai will host celebratory events. For instance, the Yu Garden and Guyi Garden will be decorated with beautiful lanterns, and the Disneyland Park will have some festival-related performances and delicacies.

Shanghai Weather in October
 The weather of Shanghai is cool and sunny in October, perfect for various outdoor explorations. Besides, autumn colors highlight the city in the late month. 
But avoid visiting Shanghai during the National Day Holiday of China from October 1 to 7 in 2026, when hundreds of thousands of domestic tourists surge into the city.  The Bund in Sunny October  
Pleasantly Warm or Cool OverallGenerally speaking, in October, Shanghai experiences cozy and mild weather with gradually dropping temperatures day by day.
During the first half month, the daytime is kind of warm, with a temperature range of about 25-30 degrees Celsius (77-86 degrees Fahrenheit); and the nighttime is cool with the temperature hovering around 20°C (68°F). In some years, like 2025, the cold air arrives at Shanghai late, and the city may experience several hot days with the daily high of around 35°C (95°F) in early October. Take it easy, this situation is quite rare.
During the second half month, Shanghai becomes cool the whole day. Daily high is around 20-25°C (68-77°F), a level that makes you feel comfortable for outdoor activities. Daily low is stable at 15-18°C (59-64°F), pretty cool so a light jacket is necessary. Cool Late October  
Stable WeatherVisiting Shanghai in October, the chances of your trip being interrupted by rain are very slim. Though there are about 12 rainy days in Shanghai this month on average, the rain during these days is most likely to be light and short. 
Humidity is around 71% on average. Combined with the mild temperature this month, the air feels fresh and cozy, but not muggy at all. Sunny October with Blue Sky  
Daylight HoursIn October, sunsets come earlier and earlier, at around 17:40 at the beginning of the month and 17:06 by the end. With darkness falling early, the available daytime for sightseeing is reduced: this month, daylight hours are shortened from 11.5 to 10.5. So, you need to plan your itinerary carefully: on the one hand, make your daytime tours more compact; and on the other hand, plan richer activities for the nighttime. More specifically, night views of the Bund, Nanjing Road, and Yuyuan Bazaar are recommended to be added to your travel list. Besides, the Yu Garden opens at night on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays from May to October each year, providing you with a unique experience.
UV index reaches 7 the highest in September, and the sunlight is strong during the sunny moments. So, don’t forget to take some measures to protect your skin when going out.
Averages for Shanghai Weather in October
Temperature: 19°C / 66°F
High Temperature: 22°C / 72°F
Low Temperature: 15°C / 59°F
Humidity: 71%
Rainfall: 58 mm
Rainy Days: 12 days
Sunrise: 05:48 ~ 06:09
Sunset: 17:06 ~ 17:40
Air Quality in October
Average AQI:38
What to Pack to Visit Shanghai in October?  Clothes for the First Half of October: You can wear short-sleeved or long-sleeved T-shirts plus thin long pants during the daytime and add a jacket for nighttime tours. 
 Clothes for the Second Half of October: Thin hoodies plus sweatpants, or short-sleeved T-shirts, thin knitwear, plus thin jeans are more comfortable for daytime, and leather jackets or denim jackets are recommended to put on during nighttime.
 Shoes: As long as they are comfortable for walking, sneakers, loafers, and canvas shoes are all OK to pack.
 Others: An umbrella is better to bring just in case. During the sunny hours, sunscreen, sunglasses, and hats are recommended to wear.
Tips for Traveling during China National Day HolidayThere is no doubt that October is one of the best months to visit Shanghai, because of the favorable climate. However, there is one thing that you should note.
National Day holiday, which is from October 1 to 7 in 2026, is one of the busiest tourist periods in Shanghai throughout the year. During this long public holiday, numerous domestic tourists stream into Shanghai. Therefore, the Bund, the Yu Garden, and the Disneyland Park will all be extremely crowded - you may even find it hard to move freely sometimes. Besides, you will inevitably spend a lot more on hotels and tickets for the Disneyland Park than usual. Crowded National Day Holiday 
Try your best not to arrange the visit to Shanghai for this period. If this is your only available time, you may want to know that:
(1) October 5-7 see fewer tourists than October 1-4.
(2) Hotel rooms and tickets for famous attractions need to be reserved ahead of time.
(3) Getting up early and finishing your trip to the most popular attractions like the Yu Garden before 10:30 can help you have a much quieter experience.
(4) For trips to Zhujiajiao Water Town, you are also recommended to arrive early to avoid main crowds.
(5) Want to see the beautiful and dreamlike night view of Lujiazui in the Bund, but wish to get rid of the crowds? The North Bund, that is, the north bank of the Huangpu River, is a good alternative. 
Travel Highlights of Shanghai in October1. During the National Day holiday, Disneyland Park will give special fireworks shows that differ from the usual ones. In the second half of October, approaching Halloween, the park will be full of Halloween-themed decorations and host various related parades in addition to the special fireworks shows.
2. By the end of October, the leaves in Shanghai begin to take on their autumn colors. At this time, there are already plenty of yellow ginkgo leaves. Guyi Garden and the “Ginkgo Alley” on Jumen Road in the city center are excellent spots for viewing them. Red maple leaves are not yet abundant, but you can look for them at places like the Yu Garden and Century Park.

Shanghai Weather in November
 November marks the comfortable autumn time in Shanghai. During this month, the temperature is cool most of the time, the weather of Shanghai is stable with plenty of soft sunshine and high visibility, and the city is relatively quiet with not very big crowds, so you will have a satisfying travel experience no matter where you plan to go. Moreover, November provides stunning autumn leaves to see.  Shanghai in November  
Mostly Cool, with Some Cold Nights at the End of the Month Visitors in Shanghai in Cool November Overall, Shanghai in the first half of November is not cold at all, but quite mild and comfortable. On most days, the diurnal hours are perfectly warm or cool, with a temperature range of around 17-23 degrees Celsius (63-73 degrees Fahrenheit); the nocturnal hours are refreshingly cool at 13-16°C (55-61°F). Rare instances that the temperature throughout the day suddenly drops to around 5-10°C (41-50°F) may occur in some years.
Stepping into the second half month, the climate of Shanghai features cool daytime and a little chilly nighttime. Specifically, highs typically range between 10 and 20°C (50-68°F), hovering around 15°C (59°F) most of the time, while daily lows drop to around 5-10°C (41-50°F). 
Quite Sunny WeatherDuring your Shanghai trips in November, you can expect many sunny hours. On the one hand, Shanghai has 11 rainy days in November averagely, a relatively low level. On the other hand, rain this month typically lasts from a few dozen minutes to two hours, and rarely lasts all day.
In addition, even when it rains, you can usually still go out for sightseeing, because light rain and drizzle are the main forms of rainfall this month, while heavy rain and downpours are extremely rare. Street View in Sunny November  
A Little High HumidityIn November, the average humidity in Shanghai is 72%. On sunny days, the air generally feels dry and comfortable. However, on cloudy or rainy days, the damp feeling will be noticeable, and the apparent temperature will be about 2-3°C (4-5°F) lower.
Short Daylight HoursIn November, the sun rises in Shanghai between approximately 06:09 and 06:33, and sets early at 16:51-17:05. Accordingly, the Bund lights up at 18:00, and Yu Garden’s opening hours for night visits advance to 18:00-21:20. Daytime shortens from around 11 hours at the beginning of the month to around 10.2 hours by the end of the month. Therefore, be sure to plan your itinerary in advance to make the most of the period from 9:00 to 16:00, when natural lighting conditions are optimal.

Low Temperature: 9°C / 48°F

Air Quality in November

What to Wear in Shanghai in November 2026?  Clothes for the First Half Month: Long-sleeved T-shirts or shirts plus a coat like a denim jacket, a sweatshirt jacket, or a trench coat are recommended to wear for the upper body. For the lower body, jeans and sweatpants are proper choices.
 Clothes for the Second Half Month: As the temperature drops further, you need to wear thicker clothes to keep warm. For instance, you can wear hoodies, leather jackets, plus sweatpants; shirts, 3-in-1 jackets, plus cargo pants; or thin knitwear, wool coats, plus jeans. Thin down jackets are advised to pack for cold nights.
 Shoes: Whether in the first or second half of the month, you are recommended to pack comfortable sneakers or casual shoes - November is the perfect time for exploring the city on foot.
One of the Best Months to Visit ShanghaiTrying to find a good time to visit Shanghai? November is a perfect choice, which features good weather, beautiful scenery, fewer crowds, and lower costs. Let’s be more specific:
1. As mentioned above, the temperature is cool but not yet cold most of the time, and the sky is most time clear and sunny with high visibility this month. So, no matter visiting the Yu Garden or strolling around the Bund, you will feel pleasant and see the beauty of Shanghai clearly. 
2. With no long public holidays, November is a relatively quiet time in Shanghai, when you don’t need to wait in long lines at famous attractions and won’t feel very crowded when taking the metro. Besides, the hotels are more affordable at this time.
3. November is the time when Shanghai is decorated with golden and red leaves, forming a romantic, silent, and unique atmosphere. Yu Garden with Fewer Visitors  
Tips and Recommendations for Visiting Shanghai in November1. Around mid-November each year, Shanghai’s autumn foliage reaches its peak, transforming the entire city into a colorful world. In addition to the Yu Garden, Gongqinglin Park, Century Park, and Lu Xun Park in downtown Shanghai are also highly recommended spots for enjoying the fall colors. If you visit Shanghai in late November, places like Sinan Road, Wukang Road, and West Lujiazui Road will be carpeted with golden fallen leaves, creating stunning views.
2. By the end of November, a lively Christmas atmosphere can be felt in Shanghai. For instance, Christmas trees and other festival decorations begin appearing throughout the city, and Christmas markets pop up in places like the Bund Source. Additionally, it’s worth noting that Disneyland Park hosts special Christmas events, including festival-related parades, Christmas tree lighting ceremonies, and Christmas dance performances.
3. Don’t miss Zhujiajiao in November. At this time, the water in Zhujiajiao is crystal clear, like jelly, and you can even see the swaying water plants and swimming fish clearly. Combined with the mild temperatures and fewer crowds, strolling around here is a very pleasant experience. Zhujiajiao Water Town in Autumn 
4. This is the peak season for hairy crabs, and you are highly recommended to have a try.

Shanghai Weather in December
 Shanghai has low temperature in December. Though it is not as low as that of some cities in northern China, like Beijing, the weather also is freezing cold because of the dampness and occasional winds, especially during the nighttime. Light rain and sleet are the main forms of precipitation this month, but they do not occur frequently. 
The cold weather of Shanghai diminishes the number of people traveling there. As long as you avoid Christmas and New Year’s Eve, you can enjoy quiet trips and spend less.
Damp and Chilly Winter BeginsGenerally speaking, it gets cold in Shanghai in December, especially at night. During the first half of the month, daily highs and lows are around 10-16 degrees Celsius (50-61 degrees Fahrenheit) and 6-10°C (43-50°F), respectively; during the second half, they drop to around 8-12°C (46-54°F) and 0-5°C (32-41°F), respectively. With this in mind, you should also carefully review the following information: Cold Shanghai in December 
1. Temperature in Shanghai at this time is not very stable and fluctuates significantly sometimes. Occasionally, especially in the middle and latter parts of the month, sudden drops in temperature can occur, bringing very cold weather that is not suitable for outdoor activities. For example, in December 2023, there were several consecutive cold days, with daytime highs ranging from 0 to 5°C (32-41°F) and nighttime lows consistently below 0°C (32°F).
2. This month, Shanghai’s average humidity is 70%, making the air quite damp and leading to even lower apparent temperature.
3. Along the Huangpu River, such as at the Bund, there is usually wind. When the wind blows, you will inevitably feel colder.
No Much Rain or SnowIn December, the weather of Shanghai is mostly sunny or cloudy, with an average of only 10 days with some precipitation. This means that if you travel during this time, the possibilities of encountering rainy weather are low.
What’s more, rainfall this month is mostly light, so even if you encounter a rainy day, there’s no need to worry: only a single umbrella is enough for you to continue the itinerary. Besides, Shanghai in drizzles actually offers a unique and atmospheric experience for you. When the temperature drops below freezing occasionally, sleet may fall, but it’s usually light and melts as soon as it hits the ground. Sunny and Clear December  
Short Daylight HoursIn December in Shanghai, it doesn’t get light until around 06:40, and it gets dark very early at around 17:00. On the one hand, this makes the daylight hours very limited, lasting only about 10 hours. Therefore, you’d better get up early and try to keep your daytime itinerary as packed as possible. On the other hand, this also means you will have plenty of time to enjoy Shanghai’s vibrant nightlife.
You may also want to know that you can see and feel soft sunshine most of the time during your trip: there are about 5 sunshine hours per day on average. 
Averages for Shanghai Weather in December
Temperature: 8°C / 46°F
High Temperature: 11°C / 52°F
Low Temperature: 2°C / 36°F
Humidity: 70%
Rainfall: 37 mm
Rainy Days: 10 days
Sunrise: 06:35 ~ 06:53
Sunset: 16:51 ~ 17:02
Air Quality in December
Average AQI: 67
Packing List for Shanghai Trips in December Clothes: For the upper body, you can wear long-sleeved T-shirts plus knitwear, hoodies, or sweaters as the inner layer. Then, choose those thick and windproof clothes as the outer layer to keep you warm, for example, you can bring 3-in-1 jackets and wool coats. Down jackets are also necessary, which will be quite useful for nighttime tours. For the bottom, warm lined jeans or heavyweight sweatpants are recommended to bring. Or, you can wear thick trousers plus long johns.
Shoes: Since the climate of Shanghai is cold in December, in addition to being comfortable, the shoes you bring should be warm enough. For example, you can consider packing boots and thick casual shoes. Besides, be sure to pack thick and long socks.
Others: To combat the chill wind, you are recommended to bring hats and scarves. And, a thick mask keeps your face warm.
Quiet and Budget-Friendly Travel MonthFor most of December, Shanghai is in its slack season with not many tourists. Visiting the city during this time means you won’t have to deal with the frustration of long lines or being jostled by crowds. Instead, you can take your time to quietly appreciate every street and every attraction of the city. Another benefit of the slack season is lower costs: prices for hotels are relatively low, and you can enjoy discounted tickets to attractions like Disneyland Park and the Yu Garden. Quiet Yu Garden in Winter 
However, it isn’t quiet the entire month. Toward the end of December, specifically on Christmas Eve on December 24 and New Year’s Eve on December 31, the number of tourists in Shanghai increases significantly. December 31 is even one of the busiest times in Shanghai of the year, with massive crowds at the Bund, Nanjing Road, Xintiandi, etc.
Tips and Recommendations for Visiting Shanghai in December
1. As mentioned above, crowds are extremely heavy on Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve. Avoid these two days if you are not into the festivals. If you plan to experience the lively festival atmosphere, you are recommended to pay attention to safety during your visit and arrange your transportation in advance – taxis are hard to come by at famous attractions like the Bund.
2. For outdoor attractions like the Yu Garden and Zhujiajiao Water Town, the best visiting time of the day in December is from 09:00 to 16:00, when the temperature is not very low and the sunlight is plentiful and soft.
3. Evenings in Shanghai can be quite chilly in December. Therefore, whether you plan to admire the night views at the Bund or Lujiazui, or take a cruise on the Huangpu River to experience the charm of this metropolis, be sure to dress warmly. Additionally, it’s best not to stay outdoors too late to avoid catching a cold. Beautiful Night View of Shanghai 
4. In early December, places like Sinan Road, Jumen Road, and the Shanghai Concert Hall are blanketed in golden fallen leaves, creating a romantic scene unique to Shanghai. In addition to visiting popular attractions such as the Bund and Yu Garden, you are highly recommended to take the time to enjoy this scenery.
5. This month, Christmas markets and light displays will open one after another at locations like the Bund Source, Xintiandi, and BFC, providing you with a good opportunity to experience the festival atmosphere in this prosperous city. Besides, Disneyland Park will also be decked out in Christmas decorations.
6. In December, the Yuyuan Bazaar next to the Yu Garden will host stunning light shows every night.

Shanghai Dining: What & Where to Eat
As the locals in Shanghai put it, “Blessed are those born in Shanghai as they have the most chances to taste delicious food”. Shanghai is a multicultural city where people from different regions and with different cultural backgrounds gather, bringing their own culinary traditions. Shanghai dining is not one of the Eight Major Cuisines of China, but rather a fusion of the most appealing aspects of these other national styles of food. The catering industry in Shanghai is thriving, with a wide variety of restaurants to choose from, providing a rich selection of dishes. Additionally, Shanghai people have high standards for food quality and taste, and enjoy fine-tuned cooking. Therefore, it may be safely said that you can enjoy all the best food from home and abroad for all budgets when in Shanghai. What to eat in Shanghai? The following is the detailed information:
Shanghai Cuisine
Shanghai cuisine, also known as Benbang cuisine, is characterized by its rich sauces and spices, fresh and delicate flavors. No matter what dish, it exudes the refined tone of Shanghai people. Here you can find both the rich and savory flavors of Braised Pork in Brown Sauce (Hong Shao Rou), as well as the refined elegance of Steamed Mixed Shreds of Chicken, Ham and Pork (Kou San Si), all of which embody the essence of a well-rounded cuisine. There are also delicious street foods such as Steamed Stuffed Bun (Xiao Long Bao) and Fried Stuffed Bun (Sheng Jian Bao) to savor at any moment. Top 8 Shopping Areas in Shanghai
Shanghai, famed as the “Shopping Paradise” and the “Oriental Paris”, offers an irresistible allure that makes shopping an essential and unmissable part of any visit. Be it the pursuit of high-end luxury labels, the discovery of traditional Chinese souvenirs, or the immersion in the vibrant atmosphere of local markets, this metropolis unfailingly delivers a shopping escapade that is both superlative and all-encompassing.
1. Nanjing Road - The Most Prosperous Shopping Street
Nanjing Road is one of the most bustling shopping streets in Shanghai, stretching over five kilometers in length and divided into two parts. The eastern part is dotted with specialty stores and diminutive shops that offer a wide array of clothing and electronic items. On the west side, you'll find upscale shopping malls and flagship stores of international luxury brands such as Cartier and Dior. Along this vibrant thoroughfare, numerous cafes and restaurants are conveniently situated, affording weary shoppers a welcome respite. Additionally, there are tram lines running from one end of the street to the other, providing an energy-saving way to go shopping.
More to see:  East Nanjing Road, East Nanjing Road Shopping Malls & Restaurants, West Nanjing Road Nanjing Road, Shanghai A shopping mall on Huaihai Road 
2. Huaihai Road - Luxury Goods Gathering Place
Huaihai Road, a quintessential high-end fashion shopping boulevard in Shanghai, is home to a sprawling array of over 400 stores. It serves as a magnet for a multitude of international luxury brands. Renowned names such as Gucci, Chanel, and Louis Vuitton have established their flagship emporiums here, presenting the latest and trendiest collections of clothing, bags, shoes, and other fashionable accouterments of the current season.
3. Yuyuan Bazaar - The Grand Bazaar of Traditional Features
Yuyuan Bazaar, being one of Shanghai's historical and cultural landmarks, exhibits a distinctively unique Chinese traditional style. It houses a diverse range of Chinese-style commodities and handicrafts, accompanied by numerous food stalls. Here, visitors can purchase souvenirs that are rich in Chinese characteristics, such as silk products, antiques, jade, and traditional handicrafts, thereby enabling them to immerse themselves in and experience the alluring charm of Chinese traditional culture.  Yuyuan Bazaar, Shanghai An exquisite store in Tianzifang 
4. Tianzifang - The Fusion of Art and Shopping
Tianzifang, nestled in the French Concession of Shanghai, is a charming district where many edifices preserve the architectural essence of the 1930s. Comprising a labyrinth of narrow and winding alleys, it houses a profusion of art studios, galleries, and specialty boutiques. Here, one can relish the sight of avant-garde paintings, sculptures, photographic masterpieces, and other forms of artistic expression, while also having the opportunity to acquire handicrafts, exquisite jewelry, T-shirts emblazoned with artistic motifs, and other unique commodities. Moreover, it serves as a haven for photography aficionados, as even a spontaneous click can yield a photograph replete with artistic charm.
5. Xintiandi - The Trendy Place Blending the Old and the New
Xintiandi, a remarkable blend of tradition and modernity, as well as an integration of the East and the West. The northern block preserves the time-honored Shikumen buildings, while the southern block infuses new urban vitality. Surrounding the area, prosperous edifices host a variety of establishments such as gourmet restaurants, cozy book bars, exotic cafes, and high-end shopping malls. The nightlife here is also very rich. There are many bars and entertainment venues, which are good places for you to relax and feel the vitality of modern urban Shanghai after shopping. Xintiandi, Shanghai Prcelains in the Yunzhou Curio City 
6. Yunzhou Curio City - The Treasure Hunting Spot for Antique Collections
The Yunzhou Curio City, a significant antique trading market in Shanghai, houses hundreds of stalls brimming with a diverse range of antique treasures. Within it, one can discover antique porcelain pieces hailing from various epochs and exhibiting an array of shapes. Vintage cameras are also present, bearing the photographic memories of bygone times, and old vinyl records that enable one to savor the charm of the music from years past.
7. AP Plaza – A Paradise for Budget Shoppers
The AP Plaza is renowned for its budget-friendly offerings. The stalls are densely populated with an extensive assortment of merchandise. Here, one can encounter “substitute” items of clothing in the styles of various prominent brands, sporting diverse designs that stay in tune with the latest fashion fads. Despite their lack of authenticity, the prices are highly accessible. If the genuineness of the products is not a concern for you and you place greater emphasis on cost-effectiveness and distinctive aesthetics, then exploring this market for a shopping spree will prove to be an engaging and enjoyable experience.
8. The South Bund Fabric Market - The Ideal Place for Custom-Made Clothing South Bund Fabric Market, Shanghai 
The South Bund Fabric Market stands as an optimal destination for bespoke clothing. It presents a rich selection of fabrics, such as silk, chiffon, leather, and others, which vary in both material and color. Be it an elaborate dress, a trendy suit, or a traditional Chinese cheongsam or gown, the proficient tailors here are capable of customizing it to your precise specifications. Bargaining is a common practice in this market. You can engage in price negotiation with the tailors and thereby obtain satisfactory custom-made clothing at a more economical price.

Shanghai Nightlife
 Night View of Huangpu River 
 and the Bund 
Night life in Shanghai is gentle and colorful because life here is much more than life itself. It is elegant.
The scenery at night has to be seen and the Bund is a must. The ornate classical and modern buildings take on a new and exciting look as they are lit up by an abundance of colored lights. Looking across the Huangpu River to the Oriental Pearl TV Tower and Jinmao Tower is a magical sight. A night-time Huangpu River cruise presents a wonderful opportunity to appreciate the night life on the Bund. 30 or so boats carry tourists. These include deluxe boats, ancient dragon boats of Ming and Qing styles, boats of Shikumen style of old Shanghai, Pirate Boat, etc. The boat fare is CNY 120 for a classic ride and CNY 128 to 188 for a luxury ride. Whatever kind of boat you take, the view to be seen here at night will be sure to live on in your memory for years to come.
Leaving the scenery aside, walking westward along Nanjing East Road, you will quickly reach the famous Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street, the gaily illuminated shops are an exciting backdrop to the cheerful crowds that come here after dark to enjoy the carefree atmosphere, where it is possible to pick up a bargain or enjoy a tasty morsel to eat.
Metro Line 1 links the three main shopping areas of the city: Nanjing Road, Huanhai Road and Xujiahui. Something that is most convenient for those who like their shopping expeditions! Most of the shops will close at 10 pm but that is when the tea houses and bars really come into their own and the night is still young!
Tea Houses open 24 hours a day. Apart from enjoying a lone taste of tea, you can invite several friends and play cards or just chat. Once you are here, you can experience all this for yourself. Fashionable entertainments are favorites with young people. When night falls, Shanghai bathes in the light of various entertainment venues. Nightclubs, Karaoke, discos, and coffee houses are all popular night time meeting places.
  A cafe in Xintiandi Xintiandi has many visitors. If you are visiting Shanghai for the first time, it is much safer to go Xintiandi for the night life. Xintiandi, the most fashionable area cultivated in the distinctive Shikumen Buildings, the architectural styles of both west and east from the 1920s and 1930s Shanghai around South Huangpi Road and Xingye Road, has become the popular place to go. Every building has a modern interior and has become an international gallery, fashion shop, themed restaurant, coffee house or bar. Bars are where young white collars discuss their work or talk about life; even hard questions on the desk get solved here! Open-air bars are popular here also. Xintiandi offers the most choice and favorable appreciation. The arrival of more and more boutiques, designer shops and luxury goods stores continually adds to the enjoyment of Xintiandi.
ARK Live House is a music restaurant and music bar
Address: No. 15, north block of Xintiandi, No. 181, Taicang Road
Ven Ice is a coffee bar, located at Unit 1, No. 22, north block of Xintiandi, No. 181, Taicang Road
Shanghai's first bars were opened in Hengshan Road, and they remain more popular than those elsewhere. Close to Xujiahui Commercial Circle, Hengshan Road is situated in a convenient situation. Here there are bars in great numbers, side by side and in which you can take tea or coffee. A wide variety of bars ranging from the brash to more intimate and quiet abound to suit your every mood. Thus, Hengshan Road at night can be one of the most bustling places in th city.
Maoming South Road: An upwardly mobile bar street.
This is where the foreign guests like to stay. The old but noted bars like Judystoo are still popular with visitors. Newly-opened Babyface's business is booming. The Colors and Face clubs inside the Ruijin Hotel in the street add their own touch of splendor to this road.
Babyface is a lounge bar and often full of people as it is where young people like to congregate.
Address: No. 180, Maoming South Road Nanjing Road at night Fuxing Park, located at No.2, Haolan Road, is the only well-preserved French park in China, so people also call it "France Garden". Altogether there are three clubs here. They are Park97, Guandi and Cash Box.
Among them, Park97 is where veterans spend their nights through. Three popular food and entertainment grounds, Baci Restaurant of Italian cuisine, Tokio Joe Restaurant with its Japanese cuisine and the California Club from Hong Kong Lan Kwai Fong make up Park97. Compared with that in Xintiandi, nightlife here is not that showy but exudes an everlasting glamour. With elegance, exoticism, top-rank wine and music, Park97 has its special charm. Guandi, the most noted club here, is the first superior club opened in China after Taibei's. Cash Box (Qian Gui) as Shanghai's oldest, most renowned KTV has the largest scale. The branch in Fuxing Park is the best of all in the city.

Top 10 Shanghai Facts You Should Know
Chinese Name: 上海 (shàng hǎi)
Administration Type: Municipality
Area: 6,340 sq km (2,458 sq mi)
Resident Population: 24.8745 million (by 2023)
Area Code & Zip Code:
Area Code: 021
Postal Code: 200000 - 202100
Location: Yangtze River Delta, East China (31° 14' N, 121° 29' E)
1. China’s Largest City
Shanghai is certainly not the largest city in China for its geographical area, but it ranks China’s largest city in terms of the population. Although its total area is 6,340 square kilometers (2,458 square miles), ranking the 33st in China, there are over 24 million people living there, leading to a population density of 3,920 per square kilometer. 
2. One of the World Financial Center
Over the past two decades, Shanghai has thrived. In the top ten global financial centers list released by the Global Financial Centers Index in 2024, it ranks sixth and third in Asia. Many businesses have flourished in Shanghai, providing new opportunities for China's growing middle class and foreigners who want to enter the Chinese market.
3. A Multi-cultural Metropolis of History and Modernity
In terms of cultural and historical facts about Shanghai, the colonial past makes it unique from other cities in China.  
 a. Originally, it was a small fishing and textiles town who did not gain its identity until it was opened to foreign powers in the 1842 Treaty of Nanking. The British, French, Americans, Germans, and Russians started to move in. 
 b. The city flourished as a cosmopolitan and thriving commercial and financial center, dubbed the Paris of the East in the 1920s and 1930s. Many westerners set distinct western-style banks, trading houses, and mansions, leaving a totally different architectural legacy. Although erected during different periods in varying styles, such as Gothic, Romanesque, or Baroque, those buildings exist harmoniously. Many of the buildings we see on the Bund and in the Former French Concession were built during this period.
 c. In 1990, it was chosen to spearhead modern China’s reform and opening up, which resulted in intense development. 
 d. At present, it is probably the most evocative city for an outsider to visit all of the country. Its modern and ever-expanding skylines include the emblematic Oriental Pearl Tower, the soaring modern art-deco Shanghai Tower and the 101-floor World Financial Centre .
 Oriental Pearl Tower and Shanghai Tower  
4. 30-day Visa-free and 240-Hour Visa-Free Transit is implemented in Shanghai
China has implemented a 30-day visa-free policy for citizens of 38 countries including France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, Malaysia, Switzerland, Australia and Japan. Starting from November 30, 2024, citizens of these countries can enter China without a visa, and the maximum length of stay is 30 days. Currently, the number of countries whose citizens can enter China without a visa has increased to 65.
Also, 240-hour Visa-free transit is implemented in Shanghai for foreign citizens from 54 countries, including Canada, Brazil, Denmark, France, UK, USA, Italy, Japan, Poland, etc.
More to see: 
China Visa-free Policy
240-hour Visa-free Transit in Shanghai
15-day Visa-Free Policy for Cruise Tour Groups to Shanghai 
5. Shanghai's transportation system is one of the best in China
As one of the transportation hubs in China, visitors can directly reach Shanghai from numerous important cities from abroad by air. The city has two international airports, respectively Pudong International Airport and Hongqiao International Airport. Its four railway stations take visitors easily to their destinations in China through trains, including the high-speed trains. Moreover, the top priority to travel around in downtown is metro for its high speed, safety, and convenience. There are 20 subway lines and 1,596 bus lines operated, passing by a vast majority of famous scenic spots, like People’s Park, The Bund, Xintiandi, Oriental Pearl Tower, Yu Garden, Confucius Temple…  
 Shanghai Subway  
6. Spring and Autumn are the Best Time to Visit 
The best time to visit Shanghai is in its spring and autumn, when the climate is neither too hot nor too cold. Belonging to the subtropical maritime monsoon, spring here usually from March to May and autumn from October to middle November, are always warm and pleasant, making it comfortable to go outside. 
7. A Sleepless City 
The colorful nightlife makes it a sleepless city, which is one of Shanghai interesting facts that you should know. When night comes, all lights shine brightly from every direction. At this time, a Huangpu River Cruise will take visitors to appreciate the charm of night scenes on both sides. In addition, most people prefer to spend free time after dark along Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street, where they may have a big bargain for small products, or enjoy some snacks and street food. Despite these, Xintiandi is a favorable place for its distinctive buildings, most of which are used as themed restaurants, art galleries, fashion shops, café shops or bars. Moreover, Hengshan Road cultivating bars in great number can be one of the most bustling places there at night.   
 Nanjing Road  
8. A Shopping Paradise
Hailed as the Shopping Paradise, Shanghai offers consumers a variety of products to choose, from high-end international brands to cheap local products. The famous shopping areas include Nanjing Road, Huaihai Road, North Sichuan Road, Xintiandi, Yuyuan Bazaar, Xujiahui Shopping City, New Shopping City and Tianzifang, from either of which, visitors can always get a satisfactory good. In addition, shopping malls are worth a visit, like Department Store and World Daimaru Department Store.  
9. Shanghai is surrounded by ancient water towns.
Outside the bustling downtown area, there are many famous water towns lying around the city, including Zhujiajiao, Zhouzhuang, Tongli, Wuzhen, Xitang, Nanxun , Qibao, and Luzhi. They are characterized by burbling brooks, arched bridges, slab-stone paved alleys, waterside teahouses and white-washed traditional style dwellings. Wandering through these waterside ancient towns to experience the locals’ leisure life style as well as appreciating the living cultural heritage will be one of the highlights of your trip. 
 Qibao water town  
10. Shanghainese tend to have a Sweet-tooth. 
Shanghai cuisine is renowned for its unique flavor profile, with a prominent characteristic being its delightful sweetness. Sugar is a core ingredient, skillfully used to create a variety of mouthwatering dishes. For example, the well-known Pineapple Sweet and Sour Pork features a perfect balance of tangy and sweet flavors, and the steamed buns with sweet meat filling are also a local favorite.

1. Visa-free Policy for Traveling to Shanghai
Starting from November 30, 2024, citizens from 38 countries including France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, Malaysia, Switzerland, Ireland, Hungary, Austria, Belgium, Luxembourg, New Zealand, Australia and Japan can visit China, including Shanghai, without a visa and stay for up to 30 days. Currently, the number of countries that can travel to China without a visa has increased to 63.
Moreover, passport holders of 54 countries and regions including the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand enjoy a 240-Hour Visa-Free Transit when taking an international transfer via Pudong International Airport (PVG), Hongqiao International Airport (SHA), and international cruise ports in Shanghai.
Cruise passengers from all foreign countries can enjoy a 15-day Visa-Free Policy for Cruise Tour Groups to Shanghai if they meet all the requirements. Pudong, Shanghai 
2. Must-see Attractions in Shanghai
The Bund, as the landmark of Shanghai, is a must-see for travelers going there. On in, there is a cluster of western style buildings erected in the 1920s and 1930s. Benefiting from their different styles, they are called “expo of world buildings”. Opposite the Bund across the Huangpu River, is a totally different skyline with skyscrapers standing one by one including the Oriental Pearl Tower, Jin Mao Tower, and World Financial Center. What’s more, it’s recommended to spend time appreciating Shanghai’s other beauties, covering Nanjing Road, Yu Garden, Disneyland Park, Yuyuan Bazaar, Jade Buddha Temple, Zhujiajiao, Waibaidu Bridge, Longhua Pagoda, Old Street, etc.
See More About:  Shanghai Attractions
3. Common Payments Methods in Shanghai
In Shanghai, there are several common payment methods:
a. Alipay and WeChat Pay:
Alipay and WeChat Pay are the most commonly used payment methods in Shanghai now, covering almost all consumption scenarios. So, how to pay via WeChat or Alipay?
1). Use your mobile phone to download and install the WeChat or Alipay APP, register according to the APP instructions, and enter your mobile phone number and other information.
2). Open the app and bind an international bank card with the logos of Mastercard, Visa, JCB, Diners Club, Discover, etc. 
3). When paying, open the APP and scan the merchant's payment QR code or show your payment QR code to the merchant.
b. Credit cards:
In some large supermarkets and hotels, you can choose to pay directly by swiping your VISA or MasterCard.
c. Cash:
Of course, cash payment is also an available option. You have the convenience of exchanging Chinese yuan at the airport or withdrawing it from any ATM that is affiliated with the bank of your card.
4. Universities and International Schools in Shanghai
 Kindergarten Shanghai has several prestigious universities, including Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Fudan University, and many international schools, offering excellent education at all stages for students. We provide practical information on famous universities and international schools in Shanghai. Click here:

5. A Converter May be Necessary.
The standard voltage in China is 220V, 50 Hz. A majority of sockets are dedicated to flat double sockets or flat triple sockets. Most hotels provide converters for their guests. But just in case, packing a converter should be on the “What to do before going to Shanghai” list, or travelers can buy one from electronic stores in Shanghai.
6. Squat Toilets in Public Areas and Western Toilets in Hotels
Most public toilets are squat toilets; but a few western toilets can be found as well, like in shopping malls, scenic spots, and airports. Some places will have the prompt to inform which type of toilet it is. The toilets in hotels mainly are western toilets. Remember to carry toilet tissues for most public toilets do not provide them.
7. Free Wi-Fi is Widely Available.
The coverage of free wireless networks is extensive, and you can easily connect WIFI freely in your hotel, shopping mall, airport, scenic spots, coffee shops, restaurants, and other public areas. But sometimes the Internet speed is relatively slow, not so satisfactory.
8. Medical Services
Shanghai offers excellent medical conditions. Specifically for international patients, there are dedicated international hospitals like Shanghai Jiahui International Hospital and Shanghai United Family Hospitals and Clinics. These hospitals possess professional and amiable medical teams that offer top-notch services and guarantee seamless communication with patients from various countries. Moreover, they can interface with your insurance to safeguard your rights. The medical environment is also pleasant, allowing you to feel relaxed during the treatment process.

There are mosques in Shanghai including Xiaotaoyuan Mosque, Songjiang Mosque, Jingxing Road Mosque, Huxi Mosque, Pudong Mosque, Pudong Mosque, Fuyou Road Mosque, and Caoxiewan Mosque.

Christian Churches in Shanghai
 Moore Memorial Church
As an international church of Shanghai, it was a Christian Church established by American missionaries in 1887 and expanded in 1931 to seat more than 1,000 worshippers. It has built up a local membership that numbers in the thousands since reopening in 1979 after its closure during the Cultural Revolution (1966-76).
Mass Time: Sun 07:30, 09:00, 14:00, and 19:00
Location: 316, Xizangzhong Rd, close to Hankou Rd, Huangpu District
Transportation: People's Square Station of Metro Line1/Line2/Line8.
Tel: 021-63225069
 Moore Memorial Church      Moore Memorial Church, Muentang 
 Grace Church
Grace Church Shanghai is a Christian church holding masses in both English and Chinese. This red brick church and bell tower is part of a structure originally built by missionaries in 1910 and has since become the home of Christianism in Shanghai.
Location: 375, Shanxi Rd N., close to Beijing Rd W. Jing'an District
Transportation: 10 minutes' walk from West Nanjing Rd Station of Metro Line 2.
Tel: 021-62539394 or 62585598
 All Saints Church
All Saints Church was a Christian church which was built in 1925 by Episcopal Church in America. Being one of an international church of Shanghai, it is a typical 17th Century Church with a wooden spire steeple with main and side halls. It also has a rose window and bell tower. The red brick, triangle roof, and concrete-engraving doorpost are amongst its best features. The main hall can seat 500 people while an attached annex hall and the small hall can seat a further 1000 people. 
Location: 425, Fuxingzhong Rd, close to Danshui Rd, Huangpu District
Transportation: Long walk from Huangpizhong Rd Station of Metro Line 1.
Tel: 021-63850906

It is the largest Christian Church in Shanghai. It was built in 1925 by a couple of Americans as a place for their choir for which it is still famous.

Tour Overview
The itinerary offers a taste of China’s largest city for those on a tight schedule, where a dose of nostalgia with a modern twist enthralls and thrills. Strolling along the iconic Bund by the Huangpu River, admire the resplendent Western architecture whispering the colonial past while looking up at the futuristic skyline on the opposite bank. Take in the classic Oriental aesthetics of Yu Garden, trace ancient Chinese art and history at the Shanghai Museum, experience the traditional way of life in the picturesque Zhujiajiao Water Town, and crown your journey with a bird's-eye view from the heights, admiring this sprawling metropolis with boundless vitality. ... Trip Highlights
Personalized private tour tailored to your own schedule and interests.
English-speaking private guide, air-conditioned private car with experienced driver.
Appreciate the exotic neo-classical buildings at the Bund, and view the futuristic Lujiazui skyline across the Huangpu River.
Step back in time to explore the elaborate Yu Garden, with giant rockeries, ponds, and ornamental pavilions.
Daydream along the waterways in the ancient Zhujiajiao Water Town, dotted with black-tiled and white-walled traditional residences.
Lose yourself in the Xintiandi neighborhood to feel the fusion of Shanghai’s trendy shops with old stone-gate architecture.
